findings.title: Every provider SSE event re-fetches the whole page, with one preview request per cell and no debounce
findings.detail: The refresh() handler runs on each `provider`, `routing`, `catalog` or `reconnected` message. Each refresh calls GET /api/routing, /api/catalog, /api/providers and /api/stats/providers (computeProviderWorkload scans the DB), then one GET /api/routing/preview for every role×cell. findings.title: Catalog change history covers only the open browser session
findings.detail: The request asks for recent routing and catalog changes (what, old → new, note, when). Routing history comes from the API. Catalog history is a client-side `session` signal filled only by edits made in this tab. It is empty after a reload and never shows changes from the CLI or other tabs. The Add and Edit form's 'notes' field is the model's own notes, not a change note. The API has no catalog history, so the request is only partly met. This gap should be called out, or fixed with a small server-side history.

findings.title: Retry prefill silently pins every role to its current policy chain when the run had no per-run models
findings.detail: When run.models is empty, the picker prefills every role with the effective chain for the run's complexity (or 'medium' when complexity is null) and submits all of them as the replacement map. Per-run chains apply to all cells and bypass operator, policy and minTier logic. An operator who only wants to change `implement` therefore pins triage, spec, review and the other roles to a frozen chain, which may also come from the wrong complexity cell. A run that had a partial models map is prefilled only with its own roles, so the behaviour is inconsistent.

findings.failure_scenario: Several runs are active and invocations start or finish every few hundred ms. Each start or finish sends about 25 HTTP requests from the open Setup tab, and previews are discarded before they land, so the panel keeps showing '(loading)'.

findings.title: Retry with different models pins every role when the run had no pinned models
findings.detail: When `run.models` is empty, the picker is prefilled with the current effective chain for every RUN_ROLE, and that whole map is sent to `/api/runs/:id/retry`. `app.retryRun` uses `models` as the new run's full model map. Submitting after changing one role therefore freezes all six roles to today's chains. The retried run no longer follows later operator edits, eval updates, or the complexity triage picks for the new run (the prefill uses the old run's complexity cell). This works against the feature's purpose of rerouting around exhausted subscriptions.

findings.title: Status reports a stale review-round or needs_human state over a newer approval
findings.detail: `explainStatus` looks at `run.status === 'needs_human'` and at the last review round's status (`waiting_input`, `needs_human`, `failed`, `cancelled`) before it looks at `review.approval`. But `submitReview` accepts an approve verdict on owners that are `needs_human`, and once any earlier round is terminal (failed or cancelled). It only refuses while a round is still active. So after a human approves the current head, the run's status or the old round's status still wins. `limitless_status` then says "Input needed" or "Review changes failed" and tells the agent to inspect the round, when the right next action is `limitless_land`. The tests only cover rounds with no later approval.

findings.title: Session-start digest makes sequential per-run detail requests over the whole unacked feed
findings.detail: For every distinct runId in the retained feed after the cursor, digest sequentially calls GET /api/runs/:id (full RunDetail including stages/invocations/artifacts) plus GET /api/land when the run has a PR. The documented hook uses --consumer claude, but agents ack through limitless_feed_ack with whatever consumer they choose, and the digest never acks. So the backlog for 'claude' commonly stays at cursor 0 and the whole retained feed is re-scanned every session.

findings.title: Quoting does not escape bidi override or zero-width characters in untrusted PR text
findings.detail: quote() relies on JSON.stringify plus escaping U+007F–U+009F and U+2028/2029. Bidi controls (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200F, U+FEFF) pass through unescaped into the session context, so a hostile PR title can visually reorder or hide text inside the quotes.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR titled with U+202E followed by reversed text is printed raw inside the digest's quotes, showing a different visual string than the actual bytes.

findings.title: Status reports an outdated failed review round when the PR snapshot lacks headRefOid
findings.detail: approvalIsLatest requires approval.sha === pr?.headRefOid. When the saved snapshot has no headRefOid (the field is optional), a newer approval does not hide an older failed or cancelled round, so status reports 'Review changes failed' instead of the approved or head-unknown state.
findings.failure_scenario: Round 1 run is cancelled at T1, the human approves at T2 > T1, and the prSnapshot has no headRefOid: limitless_status returns 'Review changes cancelled' and tells the agent to inspect the round before submitting another verdict.

findings.detail: Each row prints the full quoted title and summary; for questions, the summary is replaced with the full open question text. JSON quoting keeps a row on one line, so the 20-line limit holds. But nothing limits how long a row is. Output from a SessionStart hook goes into the agent's context, so a multi-kilobyte question or a long PR title (untrusted text) produces a very large digest.

findings.title: Digest makes one or two HTTP calls per distinct run with no limit
findings.detail: For every distinct run in the candidate groups, the digest fetches `/api/runs/:id`, and also `/api/land?run=` when the run has a PR. Those calls happen one after another. The hook's `claude` consumer is never acknowledged by the digest itself and may not match the consumer the agent acks with. In that case the cursor stays at 0, the whole retained feed is rescanned at every session start, and the number of calls grows with the history.
findings.failure_scenario: An install with several hundred runs that have PRs never acks the `claude` consumer. Each SessionStart makes hundreds of sequential requests and may approach the hook timeout.

Every state and nextAction string is a fixed literal, apart from interpolated land-state enum values and run IDs, so they could be returned safely even without the policy.

findings.title: Digest lists an approved PR as awaiting review when the PR head has never been observed
findings.detail: The review group is actionable when `approval.sha !== pr?.headRefOid`. If no PR snapshot is saved, headRefOid is undefined, so an approved PR with a current approval still appears under 'PRs awaiting review'. A test ('keeps a newly delivered unobserved PR eligible') shows this is a deliberate choice for unobserved PRs. Still, it reports a valid approval as review-needed, whereas limitless_status reports 'PR state unknown' for the same state.
findings.failure_scenario: A run has a non-stale approval, but the GitHub poller has not saved a snapshot yet. The digest counts it under 'PRs awaiting review'.

findings.title: Digest lines have no length cap, so 20 lines can still carry a lot of untrusted text
findings.detail: Each row includes the full quoted title and summary, such as question text or a run error. The output stays within 20 lines, but one line can be very long and is injected into the session context at SessionStart.

findings.title: limitless_status leaves out state and nextAction when the privacy policy fails to load

The run id, the plain-language state and nextAction are all gone, and nothing tells the agent the response was cut down. The state and nextAction strings are fixed templates plus enum values and run ids that the server generates. They could still be returned safely; only land.reason needs to be dropped.

findings.title: Digest lists PRs as awaiting review while a changes round is still running
findings.detail: The 'PRs awaiting review' check looks only at whether an approval exists and is fresh, and at the land state. Requesting changes marks the approval stale and starts a round run. Until that round delivers, the PR still counts as awaiting review, even though the factory is working on it. limitless_status handles this case and reports 'Review changes in progress', so the two commands disagree.

findings.title: One failed detail or land lookup aborts the whole digest
findings.detail: Digest fetches /api/runs/:id and /api/land?run= one item at a time, with no per-item error handling. If any single run lookup fails (the run was removed, or a transient error), the SessionStart hook prints nothing useful and exits with an error. With a large backlog it also makes many requests one after another at session start.

findings.title: Source changes exceed the requested budget by about 2x

findings.detail: The status schema drops run.merged, and the merged-state check never considers it. findings.title: Privacy-policy failure now hides results of every existing MCP tool, including mutations
findings.detail: Every tool output now goes through loadOutputPrivacy(). If private-strings.txt cannot be read, every tool except status returns only {message: 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.'}. That includes create_run, cancel_run, answer_question, review and land, which still carry out the mutation. The caller loses the created run id or the land entry and cannot tell whether the call worked, which invites a duplicate retry. Before this change these existing tools returned their results.

Both strings are hard-coded enum-like text, apart from the `round.runId` and `land.state` parts that are interpolated into them. The tool description does not mention this degraded shape.

findings.detail: quote() uses JSON.stringify and also escapes U+007F–U+009F and U+2028/2029. Bidi overrides (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters pass through unchanged. A PR title can visually reorder or hide parts of the quoted line in the terminal and in the SessionStart context, which weakens the 'quoted untrusted text' guarantee.

findings.title: Approved PRs with no saved PR snapshot are listed as awaiting review

findings.title: Unrequested change to the private-string gate decoder, and the change exceeds the ~200-line budget
findings.detail: The publication gate now decodes `\uXXXX` escapes in every scanned text, not only in the new MCP and digest output. This is stricter, so false positives become more likely in code that contains literal Unicode escapes. It falls outside the requested scope. Together with the new privacy layer applied to every MCP tool, source changes total about 450 lines against a budget of about 200.
findings.failure_scenario: A diff contains a literal string such as "Acme" while "Acme" is in private-strings.txt. Publication is now blocked where it was not before.

findings.title: Digest lists PRs as awaiting review while their run is still in progress
findings.detail: The 'PRs awaiting review' filter checks only that the run is not resolved, cancelled or merged, that a PR exists, that the PR is not closed, and the approval and land state. It does not require the run to be finished. submitReview refuses any owner whose status is not succeeded or needs_human. So a run that opened its PR and is still running (CI wait, verify) shows up as review-ready, and a review verdict would be refused with 409. explainStatus handles this case as 'Work pending', so the two tools disagree.

findings.detail: privateMatches now also decodes literal \uXXXX escapes. That function is the shared publication gate used by the engine, not only the new output privacy. The change alters gate behaviour for all runs, which may block content that previously passed. Combined with the new private-output layer applied to every existing MCP tool, the diff goes well beyond the ~200-line budget and the stated feature.

findings.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate; it blocks text that needs exactly 5 decode rounds, even with an empty denylist
findings.detail: privateMatches is the shared denylist check used by the publication gates (audit.ts, engine checkPrivateText, repos.ts blob scan, github-notifier, land queue). The diff makes it decode repeatedly and adds \uXXXX unescaping. If decoding hasn't settled after 5 rounds, it returns a synthetic entry 0, which blocks publication. The loop also gives up one round early: after the 5th decode it never checks whether a 6th would be stable, so input that settles after exactly 5 decodes is rejected. findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` passes every registered credential to `privateMatches`, which does a case-insensitive substring match. `redactCredentials` deliberately skips substring redaction for secrets under 8 characters to avoid false positives. The new path bypasses that guard and replaces the entire field with `[withheld: private text]`. Because `createMcpServer` now applies this to the output of every tool (including keys), existing tools such as get_run and feed are affected as well as the new ones.

findings.detail: Existing local worktrees can belong to the original source repository, as the surrounding code and existing compatibility test explicitly support. Output: `error: Unsafe worktree Git administration`, caused by the assertion at legacy.ts:47. This check uses real Git and registration code, isolating only the repository-lock dependency.

findings.title: Security tests can be rerun when their names occur after the first error line
findings.detail: The security guard examines only the check name, job name, and one selected signature line. It ignores security test names elsewhere in the log, although transient detection scans the entire log. A generic test job can therefore rerun security tests and record them in the flake ledger, violating the explicit exclusion. Targeted command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-yRua1O/claude-501/ci-review.test.ts`. Output for the security fixture: `Expected: 0; Received: 1` rerun POST.
findings.failure_scenario: A job named test logs `error: test suite failed`, followed by `FAIL security/authorization.test.ts` and `Test timed out after 1000ms`. The signature selects the generic first line, unsafe is false, and the job is rerun.

The classifier then throws on every inspection rather than recording its result. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". The fixture supplied a successful originating job in attempt 2 and another job in attempt 3; output was "error: Ambiguous CI rerun job".

findings.title: Completed skipped or neutral reruns never resolve

A skipped or neutral rerun remains rerunning permanently, and a SUCCESS rollup repeatedly returns false. Direct check `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `Skipped rerun: {"done":false,"outcome":"rerunning","feed":0}` and `ASSERTION FAILURE: completed skipped rerun must resolve pending inspection` (`false !== true`).
findings.failure_scenario: A failed job is rerun, but its job condition excludes subsequent attempts, so attempt 2 completes as skipped and the rollup becomes SUCCESS. The original ledger row remains rerunning and REST inspection continues indefinitely across restarts.

findings.failure_scenario: A non-security check fails on both main and a factory PR; the PR closes before main recovers, leaving no ledger record of its failure.

findings.title: Reconciliation loses results when a later attempt reruns another job
findings.detail: Reconciliation reads only the workflow's latest attempt. Partial job reruns can leave the originating job's completed result in an earlier attempt while the latest attempt contains another job. The missing name is then treated as ambiguous forever, preventing flake recording and further classification. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-sHSr7q/claude-501/ci-review/probe.ts latest`. With the original job succeeding in attempt 2 and another job succeeding in attempt 3, output was `Later unrelated attempt: Ambiguous CI rerun job outcome: rerunning` and `ASSERTION FAILED: a successful rerun in attempt 2 is never read after an unrelated attempt 3`.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A from attempt 1; A succeeds in attempt 2. Before the next inspection, another job is rerun in attempt 3. GitHub reports run_attempt=3, whose jobs omit A, leaving A's ledger outcome permanently rerunning despite its successful same-SHA rerun.

findings.title: An older probe can overwrite discovery after provider re-enablement
findings.detail: Probe results have no generation or ordering guard. Disabling and re-enabling a provider starts another probe, but the previous probe can finish afterward and replace the newer served list in memory and SQLite. The new probe records new-build, then the older body completes. Routing subsequently skips new-build and permits the obsolete build until another probe succeed

findings.title: Answered questions remain in the needs-you digest
findings.detail: Answering a question emits no clearing feed event, so replaying run.question keeps an answered question actionable until the run finishes. findings.failure_scenario: A question is answered through the UI or another consumer, the run resumes, and the digest consumer has not acknowledged the original question.

findings.title: Active fix rounds still appear as awaiting review
findings.detail: The digest ignores review.round_started, leaving the original PR-opened item in the review queue while changes are being implemented. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` with a real Store-created review round printed `active review round: expected PRs awaiting review: 0; actual Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0`.

findings.title: Merged PRs remain listed as blocked lands
findings.detail: Blocked lands are cleared only by another queue attempt or land.landed. External merges produce run.merged/pr.merged instead, leaving a completed PR actionable indefinitely. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` after Store.resolveMergedRun printed `externally merged blocked land: expected Blocked lands: 0; actual Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: Landing blocks on CI, a human fixes and merges the PR outside the queue, and the next digest includes both the blocked event and confirmed merge event.

findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the landed check never examines it. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` printed `persisted merge: expected Landed; actual PR state unknown`.
findings.failure_scenario: Merge reconciliation confirms an externally merged succeeded run using the fallback PR client, while no saved PR snapshot or land entry exists.

findings.title: Historical round failures override a newer valid approval
findings.detail: A failed or cancelled last round returns before the current approval is considered. The existing review API permits approving the current head after such a round, but status continues directing the agent to inspect the failed round instead of landing. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-354.ts"` printed `approved after failed round: expected Approved; landing not queued; actual Review changes failed`.
findings.failure_scenario: A fix round fails, a human fixes the PR manually and approves its current SHA through limitless_review, then calls limitless_status.

findings.title: Stale approvals permanently hide PRs that need another review

A temporary-repository probe running the exact hardened status invocation returned exit 0, empty stdout and stderr, and executed a planted marker command. Redirecting the submodule's .git file to the land clone's administration directory also executed a filter from the clone's root config. This pre-existing bypass remains in the replacement dirty check and defeats the requested post-check isolation.
findings.failure_scenario: The pinned commit contains a populated submodule. Checks plant filter.attack.clean in its local config and modify a file selected by filter=attack. The filter runs a command and emits the original committed contents. Running git --no-pager with the script's hardening flags, isolated --git-dir/--work

findings.title: Submodule status escapes the isolated repository configuration
findings.detail: Git status recursively inspects populated submodules using their own Git directories. A check can redirect a submodule's .git file to the clone's admin directory and plant filter.attack.clean in the clone config. safe_git now enumerates filter keys only from the isolated repository, so the recursive status executes that clone-configured filter. The eventual dirty-tree refusal happens after execution. Full-script reproduction command: python3 "$TMPDIR/land-review-submodule.py". Output: "land exit: 1", "land stderr: Worktree differs from landing commit; refusing to land", "clone config command executed: True", followed by "AssertionError: post-check status executed the clone filter".
findings.failure_scenario: A landing commit contains a populated submodule and a filter-selected tracked file. During checks, code plants a clean-filter command in the clone config and redirects the submodule's .git file to the clone admin directory. Post-check status executes the command.

findings.title: Provider export makes the retained runtime entry fatal again
findings.detail: The collision exception requires source="code", but `limitless providers export --write` explicitly exports built-in models and resolveCatalog then marks them source="config". The retained runtime Haiku entry consequently causes the next startup to throw `catalog collision: claude/haiku-5.5`, even when the exported definition preserves the built-in values. A direct export/resolve probe confirmed the source changes from code to config. Full Factory execution was blocked by the installed Zod incompatibility.
findings.failure_scenario: Upgrade an installation containing runtime claude/haiku-5.5, successfully start it, run the supported `limitless providers export --write --yes`, then restart the daemon. The runtime row remains stored, while the matching effective model now has source=config, so startup throws.

findings.failure_scenario: [local].remote_host is "2001:db8::10" and the remote unit is already installed. local status, up and down fail with Invalid URL before reaching the host.

Once this model is removed, any historical run pinning it makes unrelated model additions, patches and removals fail—even when its chain also contains a valid fallback. findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a JSON-escaped credential containing backslashes or control characters. The process runner truncates its prefix. The remaining escaped representation exceeds the literal-length overlap and its suffix survives in the gate result.

findings.title: Failure diagnostics no longer have a bounded character budget
findings.detail: Replacing line.slice(0, 8_000) with the entire line removes the retained diagnostic size bound. The line-count limit does not bound memory, and subsequent overflow repeatedly joins and redacts all retained text. A targeted bun -e probe fed FailureExcerpts 39 lines of one million characters and observed 39,000,000 retained characters; previously these lines retained at most 312,000 characters. Larger output can exhaust the shared daemon's heap despite the process runner's bounded tail.

findings.detail: Redaction happens separately on stdout and stderr, but joining them can form a complete registered multiline credential. findings.title: Detect signals executed inside shell expansions
findings.detail: Double-quoted arguments are treated as opaque strings, and non-interpreter heredocs are discarded entirely. Both can execute command substitutions, so real kill attempts disappear from warnings, the feed, and reports. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\""), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent submits echo "$(kill -TERM 123)" or an unquoted cat heredoc containing $(kill -TERM 123). The shell attempts the signal, but neither harness emits a warning.

findings.title: Preserve executable JavaScript template interpolations
findings.detail: jsSignal removes entire template literals, including executable ${...} expressions. A process.kill call inside an interpolation is therefore missed in both shell-invoked JavaScript and JavaScript tools. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("node -e '\''console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'\''"), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent runs node -e 'console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'. JavaScript attempts the signal, but the event log and report contain no signal warning.

findings.title: Provide writable isolated state for the confined Codex CLI

findings.title: Preserve the exemption for PNGs with ordinary metadata

Ordinary image metadata was not excluded by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A PNG exported with a title, copyright notice, or embedded color profile blocks without Allow: binary.

A local probe with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 confirmed that `git config --get credential.helper` returned `trusted-helper` before isolation, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh <capture> push https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/test` queried the same effective setting and returned exit 1 with empty output.
findings.failure_scenario: The global config selects a credential helper through a hasconfig remote-URL condition matching the checkout's origin. Ordinary pushes authenticate, but delivery and landing pushes lose that helper.

findings.title: The SSH default overrides trusted GIT_SSH
findings.detail: When core.sshCommand is unset, injecting core.sshCommand=ssh overrides Git's existing GIT_SSH environment setting. A network-free probe used GIT_SSH to run a local receive-pack: `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/before"` succeeded, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/after"` exited 128 with `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` The invocation markers were `trusted` followed by `fallback`, proving the wrapper bypassed GIT_SSH.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation supplies its SSH identity or authentication wrapper through GIT_SSH and has no global core.sshCommand. Factory pushes now invoke plain ssh and fail authentication.

findings.title: Hardcoded HTTPS breaks existing SSH authentication
findings.detail: The final push previously used origin's transport and now always uses HTTPS. An SSH-only installation with working global SSH configuration gains no HTTPS credentials from that change, so landing fails after checks and the final scan. This violates the requirement to preserve existing helper or SSH authentication.
findings.failure_scenario: The landing checkout has an SSH origin, authentication works through an SSH key, and no HTTPS credential helper or URL rewrite is configured. The final push switches to HTTPS and cannot authenticate.

Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.

findings.title: Preserve trusted URL-conditional credential configuration
findings.detail: Replacing GIT_COMMON_DIR removes remote URLs used by trusted global includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:…" conditions. Consequently, credential helpers and SSH settings supplied by those global includes disappear during the push, breaking existing authentication. The HTTP-free probe `python3 "$TMPDIR/push-conditional-review.py"` printed `Before wrapper: credential fill succeeded`, then `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled`, followed by `AssertionError: trusted global URL-conditional credentials lost during push`.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes their credential helper based on remote.origin.url. Normal credential lookup succeeds, but every factory push through this wrapper loses that helper and cannot authenticate.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land queue push paths
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch receives the requested protection. Both still consume repository-scoped command settings through worktreeGit. A local probe invoking these exports with a planted core.sshCommand produced `delivery: repository command executed = true` and `land: repository command executed = true`. Command: `env -u GIT_SSH_COMMAND -u GIT_SSH bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"`. The planted command only created a marker and exited; no network was used.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants core.sshCommand in repository config. Delivery or land queue publication subsequently invokes that command.

findings.title: Config snapshots do not isolate the final push
findings.detail: The final push still reads repository config and targets origin. A surviving check subprocess can change config after the final snapshot. A local probe using the script's actual validation functions passed validation and snapshot equality, then planted core.sshCommand before the unchanged push invocation. Command: `bash "$TMPDIR/review-race-probe.sh"`; output: `After successful validation and equal snapshots: repository command executed = true`. The new checks leave the underlying vulnerability open.
findings.failure_scenario: An unconfined check leaves a background process that writes command-running config between the last snapshot and Git reading config for push.

findings.title: Allow ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist rejects harmless existing settings, including user.name, user.email, and additional remotes. This prevents otherwise valid repositories from landing. Command: `bash "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.sh"`; a fresh repository passed, but adding only user.name produced `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and exit status 1.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer configures their commit identity locally and invokes land-pr.sh. The script exits before installing dependencies or running checks.

findings.title: Adjust the integration tests' execution budget
findings.detail: `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts` failed the missing and clean final-PR cases at 5000 ms. The isolated command `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'land validates the final PR after CI: (missing|clean)$'` reproduced both timeouts and `Expected: true, Received: false` at line 850. With `--timeout 30000`, both passed in 6406 ms and 6310 ms. The added config subprocesses leave these integration cases beyond their default timeout on this machine.
findings.failure_scenario: The default check runs these cases on a loaded machine; Bun times them out and fails the suite despite their eventual successful behavior.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land-queue pushes too
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch excludes repository config or overrides command-running settings. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push.ts"` against a local bare remote with a repository-scoped URL rewrite and protocol.ext.allow=always produced `delivery: marker=true` and `land: marker=true`; both remote SHAs still matched the pinned SHA. These two explicitly required push paths remain vulnerable.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants a URL rewrite to an ext helper that creates a marker and forwards to the local Git transport. Subsequent delivery or land-queue publication executes that helper.

findings.title: Exclude untrusted config during the actual push
findings.detail: The final push still uses origin and reads live repository config. Validation and snapshot comparison only inspect earlier state; they do not prevent a background process started by unconfined PR checks from planting remote.origin.receivepack after the last snapshot. The actual push also lacks the required protocol.ext.allow=never override.
findings.failure_scenario: A background child of bun run check updates repository config after config_after is captured but before git push reads it. The push then executes the planted receivepack command.

findings.title: Do not reject harmless repository settings
findings.detail: The new allowlist blocks ordinary repository-local identity settings, preventing landing before checks even start. Invoking validate_repository_config in a temporary repository with a valid origin and local user.name/user.email returned exit 1 and printed `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and the equivalent user.email error. The request requires ignoring untrusted push settings, not banning unrelated repository configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configures their commit identity locally rather than globally and runs land-pr.sh on an otherwise valid checkout.

findings.title: Allow sufficient time for the expanded subprocess tests
findings.detail: `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts` finished with `45 pass`, `18 fail`, and `14 errors`; all 18 failed cases exceeded the default 5000ms timeout, causing subsequent assertion failures. Running `bun test --timeout 30000 test/land-pr.test.ts -t 'tampering: redirect$'` passed in 8130ms. The four receivepack/SSH/helper/include cases also passed with the longer timeout, taking 6.7–8.1 seconds each.
findings.failure_scenario: The normal test command runs these expanded cases on a slower or loaded macOS machine and terminates them before validation or publication completes.

A process left running by the unconfined checks can install receivepack or pushurl after the snapshot. The local probe `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.py"` used the script's actual functions and emulated that write between comparison and push. It printed `post-snapshot-write: exit 0` and `repository receivepack executed = True ; exact SHA = True`. Thus the pinned SHA does not prevent command execution in the protected window.

findings.title: The allowlist blocks landing repositories with harmless local settings
findings.detail: The validator rejects every local key outside a narrow clone-metadata list, including ordinary user.name, user.email, and additional remotes. This changes normal landing behavior instead of excluding untrusted config only for the push. Running `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.py"` with local user.name printed `local-identity: exit 1`, `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land`, and `Cannot validate repository git config; refusing to land`. The script stops before checks or publication even though this setting cannot execute a push command.

gold.summary: The loop detector aborts before the threshold call can return evidence of progress.

findings.title: The sixth call aborts before its changed result can establish progress
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before receiving the current result. Both harnesses immediately abort and retain stuckReason, so observeResult() cannot rescue the run. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"waiting");} console.log(d.observe("shell","poll","5"));d.observeResult("5","progress");' Output: repeated the same shell call 6 times. The changed sixth result should restart the count.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'; the sixth poll returns 'progress'. The harness aborts at the sixth call before considering its changed result.

findings.title: Late results overwrite the baseline of newer identical calls
findings.detail: results stores the last completion rather than the previous identical call in invocation order. An older completion can replace a newer hash, causing the next unchanged result to clear the window incorrectly. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100);for(let i=1;i<=3;i++)d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult("1","A");d.observeResult("3","B");d.observeResult("2","A");for(let i=4;i<=9;i++){const r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"B");if(i===9)console.log(r);}' Output: null. Calls 4–9 repeat result B after call 3 established B, so the sixth repetition should stop.
findings.failure_scenario: Identical calls 1–3 produce A, A, B but complete in order 1, 3, 2. Calls 4–9 all produce B. Call 4 is incorrectly classified as progress, delaying loop detection.

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call's result before declaring a loop
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before the current call's result arrives. Both harnesses immediately abort on that reason, so observeResult() cannot rescue a changed sixth result. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) { const reason=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),i<5?"waiting":"progress"); if(i===5 && reason) throw new Error(reason); }'. Output: error: repeated the same shell call 6 times. The added tests change results before reaching this boundary and miss the defect.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent polls a test log five times with unchanged output; the sixth poll would report newly completed tests. Both harnesses abort at the sixth tool_call before receiving that progress.

findings.failure_scenario: Calls 1 and 2 return A, call 3 returns B, but completion order is 1, 3, 2. Calls 4 through 9 all return B. Call 4 is incorrectly treated as another change, so six unchanged calls fail to trip the detector.

Six identical unresolved calls therefore never stop the active invocation. Subsequent calls can evict them before finish(), permanently losing the loop. gold.summary: Unresolved tool calls accumulate without a bound during a live invocation.

findings.title: Unresolved calls no longer trigger live loop detection
findings.detail: Every unresolved call is excluded until finish(), and also blocks subsequent completions of its key. Repeated calls with missing results can therefore continue until the tool budget or timeout, contrary to the requirement that still-running calls retain today's counting. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); let r=null; for(let i=0;i<6;i++) r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); console.log(r); if(r===null) throw Error("missing-result loop undetected");'` prints `null` and fails with `error: missing-result loop undetected`. Twenty unresolved identical calls likewise return no reason.
findings.failure_scenario: An active agent emits six or more identical tool calls with distinct IDs and no results. Neither harness aborts at the existing repetition threshold; calls can continue until the separate budget or timeout.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: Out-of-order results can stop calls whose outputs all differ
findings.detail: Only the last call's unresolved result delays detection. If six parallel identical calls complete in reverse order, the sixth call's result immediately triggers a stop before the preceding results can establish progress. Both harnesses abort on that verdict. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as a } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++) d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); a.equal(d.observeResult("5", "5"), null);' Output: AssertionError: actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null. Feeding equivalent real-shaped Claude events reproduces the same failure.
findings.failure_scenario: Six identical calls are issued concurrently, with respective outputs 0 through 5. Call 5 completes first; the detector returns stuck immediately and the harness cancels the invocation before the remaining distinct results arrive.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: An unresolved sixth call no longer triggers loop detection
findings.detail: This condition suppresses detection until another tool call invokes reconcile(true) or the process exits and finish() runs. If the sixth identical call hangs without returning a result, neither happens while the invocation remains active. The agent consequently runs until an unrelated inactivity or invocation timeout, whereas the request explicitly preserves today's counting for still-running calls. A direct bun -e probe with five identical completed calls followed by one unresolved identical call returned null for all six observe() calls.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical shell calls return 'waiting'; a sixth identical shell call starts and never returns. No further tool calls arrive. The repeated-call detector never aborts the active invocation.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts
findings.detail: Every observe() calls reconcile(true), treating a pending threshold result as finished merely because another tool starts. Both harnesses then abort immediately, so a changed result cannot establish progress. The new 'pending threshold result' test explicitly expects this incorrect cutoff. findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'. A sixth poll starts and will return 'progress', but an unrelated Read starts before that result arrives. The detector reports a loop and both harnesses cancel the progressing invocation.

Reproduction: `bun -e 'import {LoopDetector as D} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new D(100); d.observe("shell","poll","a"); d.observeResult("a","old"); for(let i=0;i<12;i++) d.observe("Read",i); for(let i=0;i<6;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),"new");} console.log(d.finish());'` outputs `repeated the same shell call 6 times`; expected `null`, because the first new result is progress and only five subsequent calls repeat it.

findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2. Before the next poll, another job in the workflow is rerun in attempt 3. Attempt 3's job list excludes A.

findings.title: Resolve rerun claims when GitHub definitively rejects the request
findings.detail: The rerun claim is persisted before the POST, but a rejected POST only throws. Output: `first inspection: Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed`, followed by three `later inspection complete: false` lines and `{"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}`.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
findings.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's entire observation loop. Later PRs are skipped even though their GraphQL snapshots were fetched successfully. findings.title: Definitively rejected reruns remain pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before POST, but every non-201 response leaves it in rerun_requested. If GitHub rejects the request, no later attempt exists to resolve that claim. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` against that fixture produced `main-status {"outcomes":["rerunning"],"feed":[],"reruns":1,"mainStatusesRequested":false}`.

findings.title: Job reruns can also rerun downstream security tests
findings.detail: GitHub's job rerun endpoint reruns the selected job and its dependent jobs. The security checks inspect only the selected job; the sibling lookup also filters immediately to that job's name. Consequently, a permitted transient rerun can automatically rerun a downstream security job, violating the security-test exclusion.

findings.detail: A rejected 429 response leaves the durable claim as rerun_requested. Because ciPending remains persisted, the same PR repeats the failure every poll and prevents later PRs from recording CI, review, closure, or merge observations. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with stored `o/r` and returned `O/R` produced `{"name":"canonical-repo-case","posts":0,"outcomes":[],"needsFix":0,"error":"Error: Incomplete failing job"}`.

Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `{"name":"test-own-timeout","posts":0,"outcomes":["failed"],"needsFix":4,"error":""}`.

findings.detail: Omitting effort preserves the old value, while sending null fails validation. findings.title: Clear stale model rejection blocks when replacing a backend
findings.detail: Catalog mutations update model definitions but leave ProviderTracker.modelBlocks keyed by the unchanged catalog ID. After a backend rejection, correcting its backend through PATCH still leaves the corrected model unroutable for up to 24 hours. Deleting and re-adding that ID also retains the block. An in-memory add → blockModel → patch → route check printed `resolved backend: good-build` followed by `{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment","reason":"codex: model rejected: unknown model bad-build"}]}`.

findings.title: Clear stale backend rejection when replacing a runtime model
findings.detail: Catalog updates replace the router definition but retain ProviderTracker.modelBlocks, which are keyed only by catalog ID. A rejection of the old backend therefore blocks the replacement backend for up to 24 hours. Deleting and re-adding the ID also retains the block. Check: `bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-review.ts" block` printed `{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment","reason":"codex: model rejected: old-build is not available"}]}` and failed with `AssertionError: patched new backend must not inherit old backend rejection` (`0 !== 1`).

findings.title: Prevent older probes from overwriting newer discovery results
findings.detail: Each probe unconditionally records its response without request ordering or a generation check. Concurrent probes can finish out of order, persisting an obsolete served set and making the router reject a currently served model. Provider enable operations can start probes alongside scheduled probes. Check: `bun "$TMPDIR/catalog-review.ts" ordering` printed `{"served":["retired-build"],"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"omlx/qwen-flash","reason":"not served by omlx"}]}` and failed with `AssertionError: late older probe must not overwrite newer served list` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.failure_scenario: An older probe captures the previous backend list. A second probe observes the replacement model and completes first. The older response then arrives and replaces the current discovery result, so routing skips the replacement until another successful probe.

findings.title: Validate runtime mutations against the underlying eval policy
findings.detail: PATCH validates only the effective policy, so an operator override can hide an eval-policy reference that the patch invalidates. Resetting that override then produces no eligible candidate. On restart, Factory reads and validates the eval policy before applying operator overrides, so startup fails. DELETE similarly checks only operator cells and accepts deletion of an eval-policy model. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pqEs0s/claude-501/catalog-review.XXXXXX.ts`. findings.title: Answered questions remain in the needs-you digest
findings.detail: The digest reconstructs current attention state exclusively from feed events, but answering a question and resuming execution emit none of its clearing events. An inline `bun -` reproduction using an in-memory Store printed `current status: running open questions: 0`, followed by `Needs you: 1; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0` and the already answered question. findings.title: A historical failed round overrides a subsequent valid approval
findings.detail: The latest round's failure is returned before examining the current approval. The existing review API allows approving the current head after a failed or cancelled round, so that round does not necessarily describe the next action. An inline `bun -` reproduction supplied a succeeded parent, OPEN PR, matching non-stale approval, and failed round; explainStatus returned `Review changes failed` with `Inspect review round round1 with limitless_get_run before submitting another verdict.` It should report that the approved PR can be queued for landing.

findings.title: Externally merged PRs retain blocked-land alerts
findings.detail: Blocked lands are cleared only by another queue request or a queue-confirmed landing. A GitHub-confirmed external merge or closure does not remove them. The existing review API refuses another changes verdict while a round remains active.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer requests changes and the factory starts a review round. A fresh session is told to review the old head again while those changes are still being implemented.

findings.title: Preserve eval resume compatibility instead of asserting rejection
findings.detail: The new compatibility test explicitly expects HTTP 400 when resuming an interrupted eval containing an unknown historical model. EvalRunner.resume revalidates the entire stored request through submit, so one removed target prevents all remaining work from continuing, including work for supported targets. This contradicts the requirement that records written before the change still resume.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted eval created before the upgrade contains both the removed model and a supported model. After upgrading, eval resume rejects the complete request with 'unknown model ID', so unfinished trials for the supported model cannot continue.

findings.title: Interrupted legacy evals cannot resume
findings.detail: The new compatibility test explicitly expects HTTP 400 when resuming an eval containing an unknown model. EvalRunner.resume resubmits the entire stored request, and validateRequest rejects the removed ID before completed trials can be reused or remaining valid targets scheduled. This contradicts the requirement that existing records still resume. A mixed eval is entirely blocked even when the removed model's trials have already finished.

findings.title: Historical model pins block unrelated catalog edits
findings.detail: Every runtime model addition or patch revalidates every historical run against the current catalog. findings.title: Runtime models belonging to the removed provider prevent startup
findings.detail: Factory construction throws for any persisted runtime model whose provider is absent from providerDefs. Before this change, users could add runtime models to the built-in provider; after its removal, those same database rows prevent the daemon from starting. The new restart test seeds enablement and speed overrides but misses runtime model definitions.
findings.failure_scenario: Before upgrading, a runtime model was registered under the machine-named provider. On the next startup, Factory throws "unknown provider" while loading runtime_models, making all runs and provider listings unavailable.

findings.title: Recompute persisted routing overrides when restoring a missing model
findings.detail: RuntimePolicy filters missing targets out of its cached operator policy at startup. Adding the missing model updates the catalog but never rebuilds that policy. The unavailable warning disappears while routing continues using fallback models; restarting then changes routing to the stored override. Reproduced with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-retired-routing.ts"`, which seeds triage.default=["codex/recovered"] and restores that model through RuntimeCatalog.add. Output: `live ["omlx/qwen-flash","claude/haiku|codex/luna","openrouter/glm-5.3-flash"]`, `unavailable []`, `after restart ["codex/recovered"]`.
findings.failure_scenario: Start with a persisted routing cell referencing an absent model, then restore that model through the runtime catalog API. The override remains ignored until daemon restart, despite no longer being reported as unavailable.

findings.title: Multiline credentials leak through lossy line callbacks
findings.detail: The process line splitter discards empty lines before calling observe. FailureExcerpts therefore cannot reconstruct a registered credential containing a blank line: output is redacted correctly, but failures retains its credential-bearing lines. Subsequent formatGateOutput redaction cannot match the altered string either. findings.title: Failure diagnostics no longer have a byte bound

findings.title: Normalize terminal formatting before the runner tail cut
findings.detail: The streaming runner redacts without stripping terminal formatting, then truncates its raw tail. Gate normalization happens afterward, when a credential's prefix may already be lost. A targeted reproduction registered `synthetic-colored-boundary-secret-409`, inserted an ANSI color sequence inside it, and appended 15,995 reset sequences. The normalized retained output was the unredacted suffix `-boundary-secret-409`. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-gate-boundaries.test.ts"`. Output: `Expected to not contain: "-boundary-secret-409"; Received: "-boundary-secret-409"`.
findings.failure_scenario: A check prints a credential with internal terminal formatting followed by enough output to put the runner's 64k cut inside that credential. The surviving suffix reaches the stored gate result and downstream consumers.

findings.title: Preserve unresolved credential prefixes before replacing shorter matches
findings.detail: Each chunk permanently replaces complete shorter credentials inside `pending`, even when those bytes belong to an incomplete longer credential. This destroys the longer match before its remaining bytes arrive. Registering `synthetic-shared-secret` and `private-prefix-synthetic-shared-secret-private-suffix`, then splitting the longer value immediately after the shorter value, produces `private-prefix-[redacted]-private-suffix`. Both outer portions remain exposed. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-gate-boundaries.test.ts"`. Output: `Expected: "[redacted]"; Received: "private-prefix-[redacted]-private-suffix"`.
findings.failure_scenario: Two registered credentials overlap, and a pipe chunk ends after the shorter credential embedded within the longer one. The runner leaks the longer credential's prefix and suffix into gate output and failure excerpts.

findings.title: Delay replacements until longer credential matches are resolved
findings.detail: Redacting each incoming chunk before retaining the overlap can replace a shorter credential that prefixes a longer registered credential. This destroys the longer match before its remaining bytes arrive, exposing its suffix in the final gate result and downstream storage and prompts. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/redaction-review.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'overlapping registrations'. Assertion failed: Expected to not contain "private-suffix-123456"; received gate output "[redacted]-private-suffix-123456".
findings.failure_scenario: Register both "synthetic-prefix-token" and "synthetic-prefix-token-private-suffix-123456", then emit the longer credential in two stdout chunks split immediately after the shorter credential.

findings.title: Normalize terminal formatting before the process tail cut
findings.detail: The runner redacts without removing terminal formatting, then truncates to 64,000 characters. redactGateStreams normalizes only the already-truncated output. If the cut splits a formatted credential, its surviving fragment cannot match the registered value and enters the stored gate result. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/redaction-review.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'ANSI normalization'. Assertion failed: Expected to not contain "1234567890"; received gate output "ew-secret-1234567890".
findings.failure_scenario: Register "synthetic-ansi-review-secret-1234567890". Emit its first ten characters, ESC[31m, the remaining characters, and 15,995 ESC[0m sequences. The runner cuts the credential before normalization; runGates returns its suffix without a redaction marker.

findings.title: Overlapping matches make the raw carry buffer unbounded
findings.detail: With the registered credential `aaaaaaaa`, every overlapping occurrence moves `cut` backwards until it reaches zero. Repeated chunks of `a` therefore remain entirely in `pending`, bypassing tailLimit and repeatedly rescanning accumulated output. A mocked-pipe reproduction retained all 48,000 raw characters across three writes despite tailLimit 100; registering that entire string immediately before EOF produced stdout `[redacted]` with truncated false. Sustained gate output can exhaust daemon memory and CPU.
findings.failure_scenario: Register `aaaaaaaa`, then run a gate continuously emitting `a` without newlines. The daemon accumulates the complete raw stream instead of retaining a bounded suffix.

findings.title: Redaction can corrupt the trusted sandbox startup marker
findings.detail: runSandboxed recognizes its `limitless-started-<uuid>` handshake through onStdoutLine, which now receives redacted text. Registering `limitless-started-` as a credential changes that handshake before comparison. A direct runSandboxed reproduction using `/usr/bin/true`, redactOutput true and an identity confinement backend returned `Error: Write confinement payload did not start: 0`, although the payload succeeded.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured credential contains the value `limitless-started-` (or another matching substring of the startup marker). Every gate reports a confinement startup failure regardless of its actual exit status.

findings.detail: Clearing excludeModels for every pinned verify invocation also clears the exclusion supplied by verifyAttempt for an environment-blocked retry. findings.title: Use installation provenance instead of a fixed commit timestamp
findings.detail: The commit timestamp does not establish when an installation began running the sidecar-writing release. An installation can continue running the previous release after this cutoff, creating legitimate worktrees that this migration excludes. Those runs skip registration and still fail with Missing trusted Git paths. findings.title: Discover review work when an acknowledged PR's head changes
findings.detail: Review candidates come only from PR-opened, round-delivered and approval events. After those events are acknowledged, a new PR head can invalidate approval and generate unread PR events without entering this group. A real Store fixture run with `bun run -` produced unread kinds `["pr.ci_passed"]`, approval `stale: true`, and digest output `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0`.

findings.title: Do not impose an undocumented 32 MiB media exemption limit
findings.detail: Every eligible media blob above MEDIA_LIMIT is skipped and therefore classified as blocking binary content. The request exempts these media without a size restriction. A direct check constructing standard PCM WAV headers and zero-filled samples returned `1068 true` for a small WAV and `33554476 false` for a valid WAV containing 32 MiB of samples. This affects ordinary audio and high-resolution images.
findings.failure_scenario: Adding or editing a valid 33 MiB WAV requires Allow: binary solely because of its size, although WAV is explicitly exempt.

findings.title: Restore every explicitly requested media extension
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH excludes PDF, MP4, BMP, AVIF, TIFF, HEIC, PSD, EOT, M4A, MKV, MOV, AVI, WEBM, AAC, GLB, FBX and BLEND. These now require Allow: binary, contradicting the requested list and the PDF/MP4 acceptance checks. The added tests explicitly expect PDFs to block. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {isInertMedia} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; import f from "./test/fixtures/media/files.json"; const b=Buffer.from(f["0.pdf"],"base64"); console.log("PDF bytes:",b.length,"exempt:",isInertMedia("manual.pdf",b)); if(!isInertMedia("manual.pdf",b)) throw Error("Acceptance failure: inert PDF requires Allow: binary");'. Output: 'PDF bytes: 422 exempt: false', followed by the assertion error.
findings.failure_scenario: A request without Allow: binary adds or edits an ordinary binary PDF or MP4; the audit emits a blocking binary-content finding.

findings.title: Do not treat coincidental media bytes as executable payloads
findings.detail: clean() rejects magic strings anywhere in encoded or decoded media, even when they are ordinary sample values. The parser also rejects standard metadata: a valid PNG with a CRC-correct Author tEXt chunk returned false. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {isInertMedia} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; import f from "./test/fixtures/media/files.json"; const b=Buffer.from(f["0.wav"],"base64"); console.log("original:",isInertMedia("tone.wav",b)); b.write("MZ",b.indexOf("data")+8); console.log("edited PCM:",isInertMedia("tone.wav",b)); if(!isInertMedia("tone.wav",b)) throw Error("Valid PCM WAV must remain exempt");'. Output: 'original: true', 'edited PCM: false', followed by the assertion error. Changi
findings.failure_scenario: An ordinary WAV contains adjacent PCM bytes 0x4d and 0x5a, or an ordinary PNG contains author metadata; adding or editing it unexpectedly blocks without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Keep the implementation within the requested source budget
findings.detail: The request limits the implementation to 40 changed source lines plus tests. This change adds a 1,941-line custom media parser, plus changes in audit.ts and repos.ts. Format decoding, decompression and payload scanning substantially expand maintenance scope beyond the requested extension-policy change.
findings.failure_scenario: Maintainers must support almost 2,000 additional lines of custom format parsing to deliver a policy change explicitly budgeted at 40 source lines.

gold.summary: A bare executable magic match rejects valid image bytes with an incidental signature.

findings.title: Restore every explicitly required inert-media extension
findings.detail: The exemption includes only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and ICO. Required formats including fonts, audio, video, PDF and 3D models consequently block. The added tests explicitly expect several of these required formats to block, contradicting acceptance criteria. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` with the supplied PDF and WOFF2 fixtures produced binary-content/block findings for asset.pdf and asset.woff2.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PDF or WOFF2 asset without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it.

findings.title: Do not classify readable text by embedded signature substrings
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat scans entire text blobs for short signatures and ordinary words. Every occurrence of ASCII MZ or ustar causes otherwise readable source or documentation to be removed from the text set and blocked as binary. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` produced binary-content/block findings for constants.ts containing `export const name = "MZ";` and readme.md containing `Use ustar archives.`.
findings.failure_scenario: A source edit adds an MZ string constant, or documentation mentions ustar archives, without introducing any binary bytes.

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts eligible for normal review
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is true for every changed file with mode 100755, regardless of content, and binaryPaths uses it unconditionally. This blocks ordinary executable shell scripts whose complete changes are visible in the diff. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` produced a binary-content/block finding for build.sh containing only `#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n`.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal executable shell script, or change a text script's executable bit, without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Allow ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects standard ancillary chunks such as tEXt, removing the exemption from otherwise valid inert images. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". A supplied valid PNG fixture augmented with a correctly checksummed tEXt chunk containing Author/Alice produced "metadata.png" in binaryPaths and a binary-content block.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PNG exported with author text metadata, without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Avoid output-limit failures when inspecting large text blobs
findings.detail: Classification now reads every apparent text blob through cat-file --batch, including a single blob larger than the 50,000,000-character subprocess limit. The batching condition does not bound that individual read. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-large.ts"` on a 50,050,000-byte text file with one added line printed `patch length: 159` followed by `Binary content inspection failed: ... cat-file --batch -Z ... exceeded 50000000 characters. Content could not be classified.` The block remains with both binary and gitattributes allowances.
findings.failure_scenario: Make a small, fully visible edit to an existing text file larger than 50 MB; classification fails and the audit cannot pass even with Allow: binary.

findings.title: Restore every requested inert-media extension
findings.detail: The exemption includes only five image families, omitting explicitly required fonts, audio, video, PDF, other images and 3D formats. Added tests even require fonts and PDF to block, contradicting acceptance criteria. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". Actual binaryPaths included "asset.pdf", "asset.wav", and "asset.woff2", with binary-content blocks for all three.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid WOFF2 font, MP4 video, PDF document or other omitted inert-media format without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not classify ordinary text by embedded signature strings
findings.detail: Unanchored signature searches classify readable source and documentation as binary. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". Actual binaryPaths included "notes.md" containing 'The ustar format stores archives.' and "region.ts" containing 'export const timezone = "MZ";'. Both received binary-content blocks despite containing no binary bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: A normal source edit adds an MZ string literal, or documentation mentions ustar or SQLite format 3.

findings.title: Do not require a binary allowance for readable executable scripts
findings.detail: Every changed file with mode 100755 is unconditionally added to binaryPaths, including fully reviewable text scripts. Mode-only changes also trigger this independently of content. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts". Adding hello.sh containing '#!/bin/sh\nprintf hello\n' with mode 0755 produced a binary-content block.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit an ordinary executable shell, Python or JavaScript script, or change its executable bit.

gold.summary: A bare executable magic match rejects valid image bytes with an incidental signature.

findings.title: Restore all requested inert media extensions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH contains only png, jpeg, gif, webp and ico. Every other requested media format requires Allow: binary, directly contradicting the acceptance criteria. The reproduction command and output in the summary confirm that complete PDF, WOFF2 and WAV fixtures block on both additions and edits. Tests were changed to expect these incorrect blocks.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PDF, WOFF2 font, MP4 video, WAV recording, or another omitted inert media format without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not classify visible text from incidental signature substrings
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat scans the entire blob for short signatures and ordinary words. Consequently, fully reviewable ASCII text becomes binary: 'Custard is delicious.' contains 'ustar', and a TypeScript comment containing 'MZ' matches the DOS signature. The reproduction command in the summary reports binary-content blocks for README.md and code.ts despite neither containing binary bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: Add README.md containing 'Custard is delicious.' or code.ts containing 'export const x = 42; // MZ'. Both incorrectly require Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not require a binary allowance for executable text scripts
findings.detail: Every changed file with mode 100755 enters binaryPaths unconditionally, including ordinary text scripts whose complete contents are visible in the diff. This expands the allowance requirement beyond binary content. The reproduction command in the summary shows script.sh blocked both when added and when its text is edited.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a chmod 755 shell script containing '#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n', or edit an existing executable shell script without changing its mode.

findings.title: Permit ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects standard ancillary chunks such as tEXt, iTXt, zTXt and iCCP because they are absent from its fixed chunk whitelist. Thus even a retained media format fails the requirement that PNG additions and edits pass. The reproduction command in the summary inserts a correctly framed, CRC-valid tEXt comment into the existing valid PNG fixture; metadata.png receives a binary-content block.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG containing a standard tEXt chunk with 'Comment\0A normal image comment', as commonly emitted by image tools.

findings.title: Restore all explicitly permitted inert media extensions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH permits only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and ICO. All requested audio, video, font, PDF, 3D-model and several image extensions now require an allowance. The added tests even assert this contrary behavior. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` returned binary-content/block findings for both `asset.woff2` and `asset.pdf`, using the supplied media fixtures.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid WOFF2 font, MP4 video or PDF without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it despite the explicit acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Do not classify readable text by embedded magic strings
findings.detail: Searching anywhere for short signatures such as `MZ`, or ordinary strings such as `ustar`, classifies readable source as binary. This also removes it from the text sets used to prohibit hiding text with attributes. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` reproduced a block for `example.ts` containing `export const signature = "MZ";`. After adding `example.ts -diff`, it printed `HIDDEN_SOURCE {"attributeMatches":{".gitattributes\u0000example.ts":[]},"textPaths":[],"findingsWithBinaryAllowance":[]}`: Allow: binary now permits hiding this text without Allow: gitattributes.
findings.failure_scenario: A request permits binary assets. A change adds readable TypeScript containing `MZ` and a matching -diff attribute; the attribute protection is bypassed without a gitattributes allowance.

findings.title: Allow ordinary PNG metadata
findings.detail: The PNG parser rejects every ancillary chunk outside its small whitelist, including standard tEXt, iTXt and iCCP chunks. This blocks valid inert PNGs produced by ordinary image tools. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` inserted a correctly framed and CRC-checked tEXt chunk containing `Author\0Example` into the passing PNG fixture. Output included `{"file":"metadata.png","rule":"binary-content","severity":"block"}`, while the original `asset.png` passed.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG with an author field or embedded color profile; the audit blocks an explicitly permitted image.

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts outside the binary allowance rule
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is true for every changed 100755 file, regardless of its content, and is applied unconditionally when collecting binaryPaths. Consequently, ordinary executable shell or Python scripts require Allow: binary even though their complete content is visible. Mode-only removal of an executable bit also blocks. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-audit.ts"` added a 0755 script containing `#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n`; output included `{"file":"script.sh","rule":"binary-content","severity":"block"}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal executable text script, or chmod it from 0755 to 0644, without Allow: binary; the audit incorrectly blocks the change.

gold.summary: Detached descendants survive invocation cleanup and keep modifying the worktree.
Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.
Discarding changes replaces the cleanup error that should trigger round recovery.

findings.title: Process-group termination still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.failure_scenario: An agent launches a background writer using a detached subprocess or setsid(), then exits or is stopped. runProcess returns while that writer remains alive and can race git clean.

findings.title: Cleanup failures from the finally block still fail the run
findings.detail: The handler recognizes only WorktreeCleanError from the initial checkoutCommitted call. The unconditional discardChanges in the gates' finally block uses git clean -fdq without retry and throws an ordinary CommandError. That bypasses this handler even after a stuck implementer. Its exception can also replace an initial WorktreeCleanError, defeating the new recovery path.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer's partial changes reach gates. Gates leave an untracked output directory and the final git clean -fdq fails once. The run fails immediately instead of retrying cleanup or proceeding to another implementation round.

findings.title: Final cleanup can bypass the new round-failure recovery
findings.detail: The gates callback always awaits discardChanges in finally. If the retried clean leaves nonignored files and discardChanges also fails, its ordinary CommandError replaces WorktreeCleanError. This catch rethrows it, failing the run instead of advancing the round. Isolated reproduction using the real Git helpers: `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts"` reported `cleanup error reaching round catch: CommandError Command failed (1): git clean -fdq` and `Expected constructor: WorktreeCleanError`.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer's clean fails twice while nonignored files remain; the finally block attempts git clean -fdq against those files and fails again. The run terminates rather than starting another implementation round.

findings.title: Process-group termination still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: killTree only signals the invocation's original process group. A descendant that starts another session or detached process group survives, and the new wait returns immediately when the original group disappears. This preexisting limitation leaves the requested whole-process-tree fix incomplete. In `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts"`, a Python background writer calling os.setsid() survived runProcess returning: `expect(received).toThrow()` failed with `Received value: true` for process.kill(writerPid, 0).
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a background writer through a tool that creates a separate session or detached process group. The invocation exits or is stopped, but the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

findings.title: Process-group termination still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: killTree signals only the invocation's original process group. A descendant started in another session survives, and the new exit handler returns without waiting when the original group is gone. This existing limitation remains unfixed, violating the requested whole-process-tree guarantee. Exact reproduction: bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import assert from "node:assert/strict"; const py="import subprocess; p = subprocess.Popen([\"/bin/sleep\", \"30\"], start_new_session=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL); print(p.pid, flush=True)"; const r=await runProcess({cmd:["python3","-c",py],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env})
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer or its test runner spawns a background writer with a new session/process group and redirects its output. The invocation exits or is stopped, runProcess returns, and worktree cleanup races the surviving writer.

findings.title: Final cleanup can mask the recoverable cleanup error
findings.detail: After checkoutCommitted exhausts both clean attempts, the gates finally block still calls discardChanges. If an untracked file remains undeletable, that function's clean throws CommandError, replacing WorktreeCleanError. This catch then rethrows it and fails the run. A temporary fake-git fixture reproduced the exact try/finally sequence. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-nUbs7Q/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-nUbs7Q/claude-501/review-377/cleanup.ts`. Output: `Gates catch receives: CommandError`, `Round recovery applies: false`, `AssertionError: cleanup failure must stay recoverable as a round failure`.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer leaves an untracked file that both clean attempts cannot remove. The final discardChanges also fails to remove it, so the run fails instead of retrying or escalating the round.

findings.title: Process-group cleanup still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: The new cleanup only signals and checks the original process group. Descendants that create another session or process group survive invocation completion. This existing limitation leaves the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-nUbs7Q/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-nUbs7Q/claude-501/review-377/detached.ts`. The fixture launches a Python child with start_new_session=True and redirected stdio. Output: `Invocation exit: 0 ; detached child alive after return: true`, followed by `AssertionError: background descendant must not outlive invocation`. The fixture killed its surviving child afterward.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer's tool launches a detached background writer. The agent exits or is stopped, but the writer survives and continues changing worktree files during cleanup.
