findings.title: Children that clear their environment survive invocation cleanup
findings.detail: Session/group membership is considered only when environment data is hidden. A descendant with a readable, nonempty environment that omits the invocation markers is ignored, even in the invocation's process group. A standalone reproduction spawned a Bun background writer with env: {FOO: 'bar'}; runProcess returned successfully while it continued writing. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501/review-process.ts. Output: {"exitCode":0,"descendantAliveAfterReturn":true} followed by {"continuedWriting":true}. The Linux implementation likewise relies exclusively on environ
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a background command with a sanitized environment, such as through env -i or an explicit spawn environment, then exits or stalls. The writer survives and races worktree cleanup.

findings.title: Directory-based orphan detection selects unrelated processes
findings.detail: Birth time, orphan status, and a shared working directory do not establish invocation ownership. This fallback selects unrelated platform processes launched during the invocation, and stopMarkedProcesses then signals them. A standalone reproduction launched an unmarked orphan shell independently of the invocation and scanned with an unrelated marker. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501/review-orphan.ts. Output: {"unrelatedOrphanSelectedForTermination":true}.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another tool launches an orphan platform process in the same checkout directory. Invocation shutdown selects and kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
findings.detail: A newly orphaned platform process is classified as belonging to the invocation solely because it started later and shares its working directory. Shutdown consequently kills unrelated background jobs. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-process-boundaries.test.ts". Output: "invocation exit 0 unrelated orphan alive false", followed by "Expected: true; Received: false". The corresponding base-commit check passes.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached /bin/sleep in the same directory and exits. When the invocation finishes, shutdown kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Preserve process-group membership when descendants replace their environment
findings.detail: Session/group membership is accepted only when the environment is hidden. A descendant with a visible explicit environment lacking the invocation markers is excluded, even when it remains in the invocation's process group. runProcess then returns successfully while the writer continues running. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-process-boundaries.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'same-group'. Output: "invocation exit 0 same-group descendant alive true", followed by "Expected: false; Received: true". After allowing 100 ms for signal delivery, the same check passes against the base implementation.

findings.detail: Process-group membership is considered only when environment data is absent. findings.title: Working-directory heuristic selects unrelated processes for termination
findings.detail: A hidden orphan is classified as an invocation member solely because it was born after invocation start and has a cwd under an invocation root. Neither condition proves ancestry or ownership by that invocation. stopMarkedProcesses sends termination signals to every returned PID. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-SWqZR5/claude-501/review-unrelated-orphan.ts`. Output: `{"selectedForTermination":true}` followed by `error: ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must not be selected for termination`. The check only inspected selection; it did not let the implementation signal the unrelated process.

findings.title: Directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
findings.detail: The orphan fallback identifies any hidden-environment process born during the invocation and running under its working directory as a member. The added scratch test manually populates the set, bypassing this missing wiring. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" scratch. findings.detail: A hidden orphan born during an invocation is treated as its descendant solely because its cwd is inside the invocation directory. This does not establish ancestry. I launched an independent process from the reviewer, orphaned it while an invocation was running, and observed shutdown kill it. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" unrelated`. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated","exitCode":0,"alive":false}` followed by `error: unrelated orphan was killed`.
findings.failure_scenario: An unrelated launcher starts a detached, environment-hidden process in the same checkout during an invocation and exits. Invocation shutdown classifies that orphan as owned and kills it.

findings.title: Detached descendants can still survive confirmed shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery starts at termination, so a detached descendant whose parent has exited, whose environment lacks the marker, and whose cwd is outside the recorded roots is missed. runProcess returns successfully while it remains alive, leaving the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" leak`. Output: `{"mode":"leak","exitCode":0,"alive":true}` followed by `error: descendant survived confirmed shutdown`. The fixture spawned detached `/bin/sleep` with `env:{}` and cwd TMPDIR.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a detached writer with a replacement environment and temporary cwd, then exits. The writer uses absolute paths into the checkout and continues writing while cleanup runs.

gold.summary: Pre-aborted shutdown with failed leader inspection references timer cleanup before initialization and never settles.

findings.title: Working directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
findings.detail: The orphan fallback selects unrelated processes solely because they were born during the invocation and share its working directory. Shutdown then signals them. A separate, unmarked launcher reproduced this with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-orphan.ts"`: output was `{"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedControlPid":33510,"unrelatedControlAlive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: an invocation killed an orphan started by a separate launcher without invocation markers`.
findings.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts an unmarked background shell in the same checkout and exits. Invocation shutdown kills that unrelated shell.

findings.title: Children that replace their environment can escape shutdown
findings.detail: Linux discovery requires inherited environment markers and removes the previous process-group kill, so even ordinary same-group children with a replaced environment can survive. Darwin also misses detached descendants with a nonempty replacement environment once their parent exits. `bun "$TMPDIR/review-scrubbed.ts"` reproduced the Darwin case: `{"invocationExit":0,"writerPid":37518,"writerAliveAfterReturn":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached descendant with a replaced environment outlived invocation`. Shutdown reports success while the writer remains active.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a background writer with `env: { PATH: process.env.PATH }` and redirected stdio, then exits. The writer loses the markers, survives shutdown, and continues modifying files during cleanup.

findings.title: Shutdown can succeed while a background descendant remains alive
findings.detail: Discovery misses a detached descendant that clears its environment and changes cwd outside the invocation roots. After its parent exits, two empty scans confirm shutdown and permit cleanup despite the surviving process. A temporary fixture spawning such a shell reproduced this with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts"`: output was `{"exitCode":0,"descendantAlive":true}`.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a detached writer with env: {}, changes its cwd to another directory, and exits or is stopped. The writer continues modifying worktree files by absolute path after runProcess resolves.

findings.title: Directory overlap incorrectly establishes ownership of unrelated processes
findings.detail: A hidden orphan is selected solely because it was born during the invocation and has a cwd under an invocation root. Neither condition proves ancestry. An independent launcher created an unmarked orphan while runProcess was active in the same directory; finishing that invocation killed the independent process. `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-isolation.ts"` printed `invocation exit: 0` and `independent control alive: false`.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent commands use the same checkout. One creates an environment-cleared detached child. When the other command finishes, its cleanup claims and kills that child, interrupting work owned by another invocation.

gold.summary: Pre-aborted shutdown with failed leader inspection references timer cleanup before initialization and never settles.

findings.title: Require ownership evidence before killing an orphan
findings.detail: An empty-environment orphan is classified as belonging to this invocation solely because it was born after invocation start and its cwd is inside an invocation directory. An independent process can satisfy both conditions. I reproduced this with a sibling launcher creating an unrelated shell orphan in the same cwd: finishing runProcess killed that orphan. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501/review-boundary.test.ts. Output included '(fail) independent hidden orphan in same cwd must survive' and 'SystemError: kill() failed: ESRCH: No such process'.
findings.failure_scenario: While invocation A is running, an independent launcher starts an empty-environment detached process in A's cwd and exits. A's shutdown discovers the orphan and kills it despite having no ownership relationship.

findings.title: Stop detached descendants with reduced environments
findings.detail: Detached descendants that replace their environment with a nonempty reduced environment lose the markers and session/group membership. After reparenting, they also miss the orphan fallback because hidden only includes processes with no visible environment. Shutdown then reports success while the writer remains alive. The same boundary-test command reported 'invocation exitCode: 0 writer alive: true', followed by '(fail) scrubbed detached orphan must stop before invocation returns' and 'Received function did not throw'. This leaves cleanup exposed to the original background-writer race.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation spawns a detached background writer with env: { PATH: process.env.PATH } and stdio: 'ignore', waits until it writes, then exits. runProcess resolves successfully while the writer continues modifying the worktree.

findings.title: Working-directory overlap does not establish process ownership
findings.detail: The orphan fallback claims any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd lies under its working directory. An unrelated invocation or user process can meet all these conditions and receive SIGTERM/SIGKILL. A standalone probe starts an independent orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess is active, using the same cwd and an empty environment. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-377.ts" ownership. Output includes `ownership: alive=false` and `AssertionError: unrelated orphan must survive` (`false !== true`).
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent operations share a checkout. One creates an orphan with an empty or hidden environment after the other starts. Finishing the other operation kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Detached descendants with replacement environments survive shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery starts only during shutdown. A detached writer whose intermediate parent has exited has no observable ancestry or original session membership. If its replacement environment contains PATH but no invocation marker, it also bypasses the hidden-process fallback. runProcess then reports success while the writer remains alive. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-377.ts" descendant. Output includes `descendant: alive=true` and `AssertionError: invocation descendant must be stopped` (`true !== false`). The same probe fails against the base implementation, so this is an existing limitation left unresolved by the explicit whole-tree shutdown requirement.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementer launches an intermediary that starts a detached background writer with env={PATH: ...} and exits. The implementer subsequently ends. Shutdown returns successfully and cleanup begins while the writer continues modifying the checkout.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve retains its default 10-second idle timeout. The MCP transport uses enableJsonResponse, so no response bytes are sent while executeReaderCommand runs. Commands lasting beyond that timeout can lose their HTTP connection, which also aborts the subprocess through req.signal. Increasing MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or tool_timeout_sec does not change this server timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite taking 15 seconds with timeoutMs set to 180000. The MCP connection times out before the test completes, causing a tool failure or cancellation instead of returning the test result.

findings.title: Disable the MCP server's default HTTP idle timeout
findings.detail: Bun.serve retains its default 10-second idle timeout. The JSON MCP transport sends no response until executeReaderCommand completes, so commands lasting longer than that can lose their connection despite the much larger configured command timeout. Subprocess stdout does not keep this HTTP connection active. The disconnect also aborts req.signal, which is passed to the command, potentially terminating otherwise successful verification.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite that takes 20 seconds. The MCP connection remains idle while the subprocess runs and closes around 10 seconds, causing a tool transport error or command cancellation instead of returning the test result.

gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.

findings.title: Restrict loopback binding to ephemeral ports
findings.detail: The wildcard network-bind rule permits binding any loopback TCP port. Restrictions on network-inbound prevent listening on service ports, but binding alone reserves a port and can prevent other local processes from using it. This violates the requested ephemeral-only restriction. The new test combines bind and listen, so a denial at listen hides the successful prohibited bind.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier command binds an available 127.0.0.1:12345 socket and keeps it open without calling listen. Another local process attempting to start a service on that address receives EADDRINUSE despite the port being outside the permitted ephemeral range.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running reader commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint uses enableJsonResponse and awaits the entire command before sending its response, so even commands producing subprocess output send no HTTP traffic while running. Commands exceeding the HTTP idle window lose their connection; req.signal also participates in command cancellation. The configured command and MCP timeouts therefore cannot protect ordinary longer test runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a local-server test suite taking 30 seconds with timeoutMs and idleTimeoutMs both set to 180000. The MCP connection times out before the command returns, preventing the verifier from receiving the test result.

findings.title: Interrupted gate completion permanently disables evidence on resume
findings.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks and gateEvidence before marking the gate stage succeeded. A crash between those writes leaves cached successful checks referencing a running stage, which scheduler recovery marks cancelled. On resume, the gates cache bypasses execution, but this new status check rejects its evidence. Neither verification attempt repairs or reruns the gates, so an otherwise passing run ends as environment-blocked.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.
Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.
Forcing HTTPS during manual push bypasses working SSH authentication.

findings.title: Preserve credentials from trusted URL-conditional includes
findings.detail: Excluding remote configuration also disables trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. In a temporary repository with a matching origin URL, `git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper` returned `trusted-helper` with exit 0. Running the same lookup through push-git.sh returned no output and exit 1. Thus existing global credential setup can disappear during delivery, contrary to the requirement that credentials keep working.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes a credential helper for repositories whose origin matches a GitHub URL. Normal Git loads the helper; the isolated push has no remote URL configuration, skips the include, and cannot authenticate.

findings.title: Preserve the repository's reference storage format
findings.detail: The isolated directory preserves objects and file-based refs but omits reftable storage and extensions.refStorage. Reproduced in a repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable`: a normal file-URL push of `HEAD:refs/heads/default-baseline` succeeded, while the equivalent push through this helper exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. pushBranch accepts HEAD by default, and the pipeline also explicitly passes HEAD on a delivery path.
findings.failure_scenario: Delivery pushes HEAD from a reftable repository. The helper makes Git interpret its administration as file-based refs, so HEAD cannot resolve and delivery fails despite a valid source commit.

findings.title: Isolation drops trusted credentials selected by remote URL
findings.detail: Replacing the common config removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. Credential helpers and SSH settings supplied by those includes consequently disappear. A local credential-fill probe succeeded normally, then failed through `bash scripts/push-git.sh "$probe" https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/test` with exit 128 and `could not read Username ... terminal prompts disabled`.

findings.title: Forcing HTTPS breaks existing SSH-only landing credentials
findings.detail: The previous push used origin's configured transport. The replacement always uses HTTPS, so an installation whose origin uses SSH and whose trusted authentication consists of an SSH key or global core.sshCommand now needs separate HTTPS credentials. Preserving SSH settings in the wrapper does not help an HTTPS push. This violates the requirement to retain existing credential setup.
findings.failure_scenario: The landing checkout has an SSH origin, working SSH authentication, and no HTTPS credential helper. Landing previously succeeded; the new final push cannot authenticate.

findings.title: Reconstructed administration loses reftable references
findings.detail: The temporary common directory preserves only files-based refs and object-format metadata. It omits extensions.refStorage and reftable storage. A local repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable` successfully pushed an explicit SHA through the wrapper, but the equivalent wrapper push using `HEAD:refs/heads/default` exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. Production delivery still passes HEAD in several paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory cache/worktree uses reftable storage and delivery calls pushBranch with HEAD, or pushExistingBranch with its default source revision. The isolated push cannot resolve HEAD and delivery fails.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.

findings.title: Preserve trusted credentials selected by hasconfig includes
findings.detail: Replacing the common directory removes remote URLs used by trusted global includeIf conditions. A global credential helper selected by `includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:https://example.invalid/**"` therefore disappears. In a temporary fixture, `git credential fill` returned username=test and password=value; running the same credential lookup through this wrapper's effective configuration exited 128 with `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled`. This violates the requirement to preserve existing global credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes a credential helper based on remote.origin.url. Ordinary Git authenticates successfully, but factory pushes lose that helper and fail authentication.

findings.title: Retain reftable storage when constructing the isolated repository
findings.detail: The isolated directory exposes only objects, refs and packed-refs, and its config omits extensions.refStorage. Reftable repositories consequently lose their readable refs. In a repository created with `git init --ref-format=reftable`, `git push <local-bare-remote> HEAD:refs/heads/control-head` succeeded, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh git push <local-bare-remote> HEAD:refs/heads/wrapper-head` exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. Production delivery paths still pass HEAD, including src/pipeline/engine.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: A checkout uses reftable reference storage and delivery pushes HEAD, either explicitly or through pushBranch/pushExistingBranch defaults. The wrapper cannot resolve HEAD and delivery fails.

findings.title: Preserve reftable references when isolating push configuration
findings.detail: The isolated common directory exposes only files-format references and omits both reftable storage and its format declaration. In a reftable source repository, Git consequently cannot resolve HEAD. Production delivery still passes HEAD through pushBranch and pushExistingBranch. Reproduced using `git init --ref-format=reftable`, an empty commit, and a local bare remote: `bash scripts/push-git.sh git push <file-url> HEAD:refs/heads/delivered` exits 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. Calling worktreeGit produces the same failure; pushing the resolved SHA succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory source repository uses reftable references and delivery calls pushBranch with its default HEAD, or pushExistingBranch without an explicit SHA. The new helper hides the reference storage, so delivery fails before publishing.

gold.summary: Manual push reloads mutable clone configuration after its final validation snapshot.
Inherited Git configuration causes validation and push to inspect different settings.
An exact upstream URL requirement rejects supported forks and alternate origin spellings.

findings.title: Protect the land queue and delivery pushes
findings.detail: Neither pushExistingBranch nor pushBranch receives the requested config isolation. Their worktreeGit wrapper still permits repository URL rewrites and protocol.ext.allow. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-JcAFO3/claude-501/review-push-l54zsh30/probe.ts` against local bare remotes printed `FAIL: repository-configured command executed` for both delivery and land. Both remote SHAs matched the pinned SHA. These existing vulnerabilities remain unaddressed by the shell-only change.
findings.failure_scenario: The checkout config sets protocol.ext.allow=always and rewrites the trusted file URL to an ext helper that creates a marker before running the normal Git transport.

findings.title: Exclude repository config during push instead of checking it beforehand
findings.detail: The snapshot comparison does not constrain what the subsequent Git process reads. Unconfined check code can leave a background writer that adds receivepack, pushurl, or another command key after the comparison. The final push still names origin and has no protocol.ext.allow=never. A deterministic probe using the actual shell functions injected receivepack at push entry: `bash /private/tmp/lr-JcAFO3/claude-501/review-shell-2o0cvp0o/probe.sh` printed `FAIL: repository receivepack ran after successful config validation and snapshot comparison`; the remote still received the pinned SHA.
findings.failure_scenario: A process left running by bun run check changes repository config between the final snapshot read and Git loading config for the push.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist aborts landing for harmless existing settings such as user.name, user.email, and push.default. This introduces a broader precondition than the requested push isolation. With only a local identity added, `bash /private/tmp/lr-JcAFO3/claude-501/review-shell-2o0cvp0o/probe.sh benign` exited 1 with `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land`.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer uses git config user.name to select a repository-specific identity, then runs land-pr.sh on an otherwise valid checkout.

findings.title: Give the expanded subprocess tests a sufficient timeout
findings.detail: The expanded cases retain Bun's five-second default despite their additional Git and wrapper subprocesses. An isolated rerun, `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts -t ': core.sshCommand$'`, failed with `this test timed out after 5000ms` and `0 pass, 1 fail`. The same case passed with a 30-second limit; all 14 config cases passed under that limit. The default file run had 13 timeouts, preventing a successful required check on this machine.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the new core.sshCommand case with the default test timeout on the shared macOS machine.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land-queue pushes too
findings.detail: Only land-pr.sh changes. pushBranch and pushExistingBranch still use worktreeGit without excluding repository config or disabling protocol.ext. A repository-local url.<ext-command>.pushInsteadOf therefore executes a command even when the caller supplies a trusted explicit URL. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"` against both exported functions printed `delivery: repository command executed=true, pinned SHA received=true` and `land: repository command executed=true, pinned SHA received=true`.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants protocol.ext.allow=always and a pushInsteadOf rewrite from the trusted remote URL to an ext helper. Delivery or land-queue publication executes that helper.

findings.title: A config snapshot does not isolate the subsequent push
findings.detail: The final snapshot and comparison leave repository config active for the push. A process surviving the unconfined checks can change config after the snapshot, and safe_git then rereads it. A probe using the script's actual functions inserted core.sshCommand between comparison and push. `env -u GIT_SSH_COMMAND bash "$TMPDIR/review-land-probe.sh" 1 test .` printed `after snapshot: repository command EXECUTED` and `pinned SHA received: true`.
findings.failure_scenario: A background process started by PR checks waits until validation completes, then installs core.sshCommand or remote.origin.receivepack before git push reads config.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary repository configuration
findings.detail: The allowlist aborts landing for harmless existing settings such as user.name, user.email, or remote.upstream.url. This changes the requested behavior from ignoring untrusted push configuration to refusing otherwise valid checkouts. The shell probe printed `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and `local identity: REJECTED`. The new tests also expect poisoned configurations to abort instead of demonstrating the required successful pinned-SHA push.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner configures a repository-local commit identity, then runs land-pr.sh; it exits before installation or checks despite having a valid origin.

findings.title: Avoid printing credential-bearing config key names
findings.detail: Rejected key names are printed verbatim, but URL-scoped credential keys can contain passwords or tokens in their subsection. `bash "$TMPDIR/review-config-log.sh" 1 test .` printed `Repository git config key credential.https://user:sample-token@example.com.helper is not allowed; refusing to land`. Thus the new failure path exposes credentials through stderr.
findings.failure_scenario: Repository config contains credential.https://user:<token>@example.com.helper; validation copies the token into captured command output or logs.

findings.title: Delivery and land-queue pushes still trust repository config
findings.detail: The requested TypeScript push paths remain unchanged. findings.title: Config snapshots leave the final push vulnerable to concurrent mutation

findings.title: The allowlist rejects ordinary repository-local identity settings
findings.detail: The new validation rejects all local keys outside clone metadata, including harmless user.name and user.email settings used by the script's own commit step. findings.title: Automated delivery and land pushes remain vulnerable
findings.detail: The change only protects the manual script. Both pushBranch and pushExistingBranch still consume repository-level command settings and URL rewrites through worktreeGit. findings.title: Config snapshots leave a race before the final push
findings.detail: The snapshot comparison finishes before safe_git push, which rereads repository config. A surviving process from the unconfined checks can install remote.origin.receivepack after the comparison. A local probe using the actual helper functions and final validation sequence, followed by that mutation, produced `shell: post-validation repository command executed=true` under `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push.ts"`. The push still uses origin and does not exclude repository config or disable ext transport.

findings.title: The allowlist blocks ordinary repository configurations
findings.detail: The validator rejects every local key outside a narrow metadata list, including harmless user.name, user.email and additional remotes. The local probe `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push.ts"` returned `benign local identity: exit=1, stderr=Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land`. gold.summary: Increasing panel test deadlines leaves the underlying parallel Git race undiagnosed.
Factory gate environment construction discards the configured test worker override.

findings.title: Factory gates strip the worker override
findings.detail: Factory checks execute with gateEnv(), which calls agentEnv() and removes LIMITLESS_* variables. Consequently this command always selects four workers, even when the daemon has LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS set. A targeted command with LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=8 printed {"parent":"8","gate":null}.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=1 to reduce contention between factory runs; every factory test gate still launches four workers.

findings.title: The new command disables factory test-evidence substitution
findings.detail: gateTestCommand() accepts only simple bun test commands and returns null for this shell expression. applyGateEvidence() therefore cannot recognize the successful suite as coverage. A targeted invocation using identical clean gate output returned status "met" with the base command and "blocked" with the new command, reporting "candidate gate checks do not cover every required verification step."
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier cannot run a required test because of sandbox restrictions, while the factory suite passes on the exact candidate SHA. Previously the engine could substitute its recorded result; after this change the criterion remains blocked.

findings.title: The required measurements and repeated-run results are missing
findings.detail: Four workers are selected without the requested 4/6/8 comparison. Neither the diff nor the implementation report supplies serial-versus-parallel wall/user/system times, the post-split top ten files, equal before/after test counts, or three successful full parallel runs. These are explicit acceptance criteria for a change whose purpose is measured suite performance and reliability.
findings.failure_scenario: The change is delivered with an unmeasured default and no recorded evidence that parallel execution is reliable or that the split removes the requested file-duration bottleneck.

findings.title: Preserve the worker override in factory gate environments

findings.title: A pinned verify chain drops the rule that the retry uses a different verifier, so the retry reruns the same model
findings.detail: For verify, chain mode sets `excludeModels: undefined`. The only `excludeModels` verify ever gets is `[firstModel]` on the environment-blocked retry (`verifyAttempt(1, [firstModel])`, engine.ts:1553). That rule is there to get a second opinion from a different model, not to enforce vendor independence. Each invoke starts with a fresh `tried` and the chain order wins, so with verify=[A, B] the retry runs A again even though the operator listed B as a fallback. findings.title: A pinned triage model's last-resort decline is discarded and the run goes to needs_human
findings.detail: `if (!target && lastResort && !chain)` turns off the last-resort path in chain mode. A decision model returns `decline.lastResort` when its answers are "sound but unsure: usable as the last resort when no other model can answer". In a pinned chain no other model can answer, and using that answer does not leave the chain, so the strict-routing rule doesn't require dropping it. As written, an experiment that pins triage to a decision-capable model fails whenever the model is unsure, even though its answer is usable.

The request says the chain wins over soft rules, not that soft rules stop breaking ties among alternatives the operator called interchangeable. The existing post-review log "Review done by the implementer's vendor (no other vendor available)" is also untrue in this case.

findings.title: The failure signature uses the first line containing 'fail' or 'error', often an echoed action input

GitHub Actions logs print each step's inputs (for example `fail-on-cache-miss: false` for actions/cache) long before the real failure. That line becomes the signature 'line' for every failure of the check. Ledger rows then record a meaningless 'failing test or error line'. Different failures at the same SHA share a signature, which breaks the 'one rerun per PR, SHA and signature' identity, and flakes cannot be told apart by test.

findings.title: A rerun is requested while the workflow run is still in progress, which uses up the only rerun and can raise an access problem

The code claims the rerun (claimCiRerun) and POSTs actions/jobs/{id}/rerun without checking that the run is completed. GitHub refuses to rerun jobs of a run that is still in progress (403). The claim is already spent, so the next pass sees the prior row as rerun_requested and emits ci.needs_fix, and the transient failure never gets its rerun. The 403 also goes through call() and ciCall, which treat it as an access problem: the repository is blocked with backoff and a 'forbidden' github.access_problem item is emitted.

The exception escapes `observe()`, which `tick` catches per repository, so every PR after the failing one in that batch goes unrecorded. `ciPending` is saved as true before the call, and `same && prev.ciPending` keeps it true. The same throw therefore repeats on every poll indefinitely. Merges, closes, conflicts and CI changes for the other PRs are never recorded, `settled` is never set for them, and `reconcileMergedRuns` doesn't run. The end-of-cycle `setGithubAccess` clear is skip
findings.failure_scenario: I ran a scratch test against fake gh. PRs #1 and #2 are in o/r. PR #1 has a failed Actions job whose `actions/jobs/21/logs` returns 410 Gone (expired logs). Then PR #2 merges. After 10 polls the log shows 'GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (410)' repeat

findings.title: Main-red pause re-fetches REST on every poll, though the request limits fetching to GraphQL changes
findings.detail: When a PR's failing check is red on main, `classifyCi` returns `!paused` = false. `record()` then returns null with `ciPending` still true, so the next poll reclassifies with no GraphQL change. Each pass reads the main commit, main's check-runs and the PR's check-runs. Main's checks are fetched again for every PR rather than once per repository, and this continues for as long as main stays red, possibly hours or days. The request says 'Fetch the failing check runs and jobs by REST, only when the GraphQL state changed.' Because `record` returns null, the mergeability nudge is also skipped and the repository's access-problem clear never runs while paused.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran a scratch test with 3 factory PRs failing 'test', main failing 'test', and the poller at 45s with no GraphQL changes. Over 4 polls it made 36 REST calls: 3 per PR per poll, without end. With 10–20 PRs at the 15s delivered cadence, this uses a large share of the 5000/h REST budget.

findings.title: Ledger signatures include per-run noise, so the same flake never matches across occurrences
findings.detail: `ciSignature` uses the first log line matching `/timed out after|##[error]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i`, verbatim apart from a leading timestamp, as the error line. That keeps volatile content such as Bun's duration suffix. It also matches incidental setup lines (e.g. `fail-fast: true`) that print before the real failure. The flake ledger exists to record each failure signature so recurring nondeterminism can be recognised, and these signatures differ on every occurrence.
findings.failure_scenario: I called `ciSignature` directly. `ciSignature('test', '...(fail) slow [5000.01ms]\n  ^ this test timed out after 5000ms.', 'x')` and the same log with `[5003.77ms]` give different signatures (`a.signature === b.signature` is false). A log with `  fail-fast: true` before `error: real problem` gives t

findings.title: The needs_fix excerpt is the start of the job log, not the failure
findings.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` sets `excerpt = quote(log.trim().slice(0, 2000))`. A real Actions job log starts with runner setup output (runner version, OS, image, checkout), so the first 2000 characters almost never contain the failure. The excerpt is noise, and the failing lines that sit past 2000 characters are dropped.
findings.failure_scenario: A typical Actions job fails in its test step after about 20 KB of setup and install output. The `ci.needs_fix` excerpt shows only runner and image details.

findings.title: Ad-hoc '> ' quoting instead of the codebase's untrusted-data convention
findings.detail: Untrusted GitHub text elsewhere goes through `quotedJson`, or is labelled with an explicit 'untrusted … quoted data' preface (`src/integrations/github.ts:48`, `src/pipeline/triage-decisions.ts`). This change adds a separate `> `-prefix scheme plus an `untrusted: true` flag. That satisfies the letter of the requirement but is inconsistent with the existing approach, and it doesn't escape angle brackets or tags if feed data is later embedded in a tagged prompt.
findings.failure_scenario: A log containing `</github-data-json>` or similar tag text is embedded unescaped if the feed item is later placed inside the existing quoted-data wrapper.

findings.title: About twice the stated budget, with dense and hard-to-audit control flow
findings.detail: The request budgets about 250 changed source lines. The diff adds about 560 source lines, 411 of them in a single `classifyCi` function with many nested closures, several throw-to-retry paths, and two migrations for one new table. The first migration creates `ci_failures` and the second immediately ALTERs it; neither file has shipped, so they could be one. This complexity makes the reliability problems above (throw semantics, pending loops) easy to miss.
findings.failure_scenario: Not applicable: this is a maintainability cost, not a runtime failure.

findings.title: Security regex matches unrelated substrings such as 'disaster'
findings.detail: `/…|sast|dast|vulnerab/i` has no word boundaries, so 'disaster', 'podcast' (no) or 'sastisfy'-style tokens count as security evidence. That suppresses both the rerun and the ledger row. The effect is conservative but surprising.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job whose log contains `error: disaster recovery test failed` is treated as a security failure: no rerun and no ledger row.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: A persistent classifier exception on one PR starves every later PR in the repo batch, merges included
findings.detail: `classifyCi` throws on many conditions (`Incomplete CI inspection` for any non-200 status, `Incomplete failing check`, `Ambiguous originating CI job`, `Outdated CI check completion`, and so on). It runs inside `record()`, which runs inside the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in `observe()`. The throw unwinds `observe()`, which `tick` catches per repository, so no later PR in that batch is recorded. The PR that threw was already saved with `ciPending: true`, and `(same && prev?.ciPending)` keeps it pending, so the same throw recurs on every poll. The starvation lasts until that PR's head or CI changes. The base code had no such path.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe test (in TMPDIR) with PR #1 failing the check `test`, where its job log returns 410 Gone, and PR #2 in the same repo becoming MERGED. After 40 polls (10 minutes of fake time), the logs show `GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/7/logs (410)` on every cycle,

findings.title: Main-red pause re-fetches REST on every poll although GraphQL is unchanged
findings.detail: When a PR's failing check is red on main, `classifyCi` returns false (`paused`). `ciPending` therefore stays persisted, and every later poll re-runs the classification: GET commits/main, the main check-runs pages, and the PR check-runs pages, even when the GraphQL `ciKey` is identical. The request says to fetch failing check runs and jobs by REST "only when the GraphQL state changed". Delivered PRs poll every 15 s, which is roughly 720 or more REST calls per hour per paused PR. Several PRs blocked by one red main can use up the 5000/h budget that the poller and the rest of the factory share.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe test: one PR fails `test` and main's check `test` is also failing. After the first poll there were 4 REST calls. After 10 more polls with unchanged GraphQL there were 34: commits/main, main check-runs and PR check-runs on every cycle.

findings.title: Failure signature can pick a passing test or setup line, and it includes run timings
findings.detail: `ciSignature` takes the first log line matching `/timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i`. Passing test names containing 'error' or 'fail', and action inputs such as `continue-on-error: false` or `fail-on-cache-miss`, match before the actual failure. Lines also keep durations such as `[5000.01ms]`, so the same failure produces a different signature on every run. The ledger's "failing test or error line" is then wrong, unrelated failures in one job collapse into one signature (the cap is over-applied, and needs_fix items are deduplicated away), and identical failures never aggregate across runs.
findings.failure_scenario: `ciSignature('test', log, 'x')` on a log with '(pass) parser > returns an error on invalid input [1.20ms]' followed by '(fail) store > persists rows [3.10ms]' returns line '(pass) parser > returns an error on invalid input [1.20ms]'. Verified with bun.

findings.title: Fail-fast cancelled matrix jobs are treated as transient, rerun, and recorded as flakes
findings.detail: Any check or job with conclusion `cancelled` is classified as transient, unless the remote head has moved. The request covers a *run* cancelled without being superseded. In a matrix with fail-fast, a real failure in one job cancels its siblings at the same SHA. Those cancelled siblings get rerun, and when the rerun passes, `failed_then_passed` is written to the ledger as nondeterminism evidence, although nothing was nondeterministic. The rerun budget is also spent for nothing. The test 'eligible cancelled failure reruns only its job' locks this behaviour in.
findings.failure_scenario: Matrix run with jobs `test (a)` (conclusion failure, assertion error) and `test (b)` (conclusion cancelled by fail-fast). `test (b)` is rerun via jobs/{id}/rerun, passes, and the ledger row becomes `failed_then_passed`.

findings.title: record() now drops the whole PR observation when the head epoch check refuses
findings.detail: The base code called `store.observePrHead(pr.url, head, since)` and still saved the snapshot and emitted feed items. The change returns early when that call returns false, which happens while a round is pushing or when the version has moved. During that window pr.merged, pr.closed, review and comment events for the PR are not recorded. This change in behaviour is outside the CI scope and is untested.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is mid-push (pr_heads.pushing set to a running run) when the PR is merged or receives a review. The poll that observes it discards the whole observation, and no state or feed item is saved for that cycle.

findings.title: Feed excerpt is the first 2000 chars of the job log (runner setup), not the failure
findings.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` passes the whole job log, and `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)` keeps its head. GitHub Actions job logs begin with runner, image and setup output, so for any realistic log the excerpt contains no failure information.
findings.failure_scenario: A typical 50 KB job log whose failure is near the end produces a ci.needs_fix item whose excerpt is only 'Current runner version...', 'Runner Image...' and setup lines.

findings.title: Multiple transient jobs in one run are rerun one by one; later POSTs may be rejected and reported as needs_fix
findings.detail: Each eligible job gets its own POST to `actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`. After the first one, the run is in progress again, and GitHub may refuse a second job rerun on a running run. A 4xx response is treated as a definitive `rerun_rejected` followed by needs_fix. The request says "Rerun the failed jobs", and `runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` does that in one call. I could not verify GitHub's live behaviour here.
findings.failure_scenario: Two matrix jobs in the same run both time out. The first rerun returns 201. The second may return 403 while the run is in progress, and is marked rerun_rejected with a needs_fix item.

findings.title: Two migrations for one new, unshipped table; change is about twice the source-line budget
findings.detail: `rerun_job` is added by a second ALTER migration, although the table is created in the same change. The source diff is about 560 lines against a budget of about 250, with a 411-line classifier that is hard to audit.
findings.failure_scenario: Not applicable: this is a maintainability issue with no runtime failure.

The other is a later release adding the same model to the built-in catalog, which is the point of trying it at runtime first. Removing a config-defined provider that had runtime models also does it. In all three cases the daemon won't start. The API is the only way to remove runtime models and it is down too, so recovery needs hand-written SQL. The add-time collision check

I ran `factory.catalog.add({...customModel, provider:'mac-mlx', id:'next'})`, then added `{id:'next'}` to mac-mlx's `[[providers.models]]` in config.toml and constructed a new Factory on the same database. It threw `Error: catalog collision: mac-

findings.title: PATCH cannot clear a runtime model's default effort
findings.detail: `patch` merges `{...old, ...patch}` and runs the result through `mapFields`. That step drops `undefined` but keeps `null`, and `modelSchema.effort` is `.optional()`, so `{effort: null}` is rejected. JSON has no way to send `undefined`, so a default effort, once set, can only be removed by deleting and re-adding the model. Deletion is itself blocked while any policy cell names the model. GUIDE.md advises omitting the default effort for Claude-backed local servers, so an operator who set one by mistake is stuck.
findings.failure_scenario: Add `omlx/x` with `effort: "high"`, then send `PATCH /api/catalog/models/omlx%2Fx {"effort":null}`. It returns 400 `model.effort: invalid or missing field`, and the default effort can't be removed while a cell references the model.

findings.title: DELETE checks operator cells but not the evals policy overlay
findings.detail: `remove` checks only `store.routingCells()`. The evals overlay from `readPolicy(opts.policyPath, this.models, …)` is validated against a model list that includes runtime models, so it can name one. After such a model is deleted, routing skips the missing id for now. On the next restart, `readPolicy` validates the overlay against a catalog that no longer has the model and fails.
findings.failure_scenario: An evals policy file contains `triage.small: ["omlx/exp"]`, where omlx/exp is a runtime model, and the operator deletes omlx/exp. Deletion succeeds, and the next daemon start fails while validating the evals policy.

findings.title: Tests don't cover decoding of the encoded model id in the route
findings.detail: Model ids contain '/', so the CLI sends `/api/catalog/models/omlx%2Fnew`, and the handler uses `req.params.id` without decoding it. The test client applies `decodeURIComponent` before calling the handler, so the tests never check that Bun's router decodes `%2F` in params. If Bun doesn't, every CLI `remove` and API PATCH/DELETE fails with `missing catalog model omlx%2Fnew`. I couldn't check this because the sandbox blocks socket binding.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless catalog remove omlx/new` sends `DELETE /api/catalog/models/omlx%2Fnew`. If Bun leaves the param undecoded, the server answers 400 `missing catalog model omlx%2Fnew`.

findings.title: Every health probe now publishes provider status, even when nothing changed
findings.detail: `probeProvider` now calls `this.publish(id)` on every probe, success or failure. Each publish also queries `served_models` through `status()`. Before this change, status was only pushed when health changed. Changes that matter are already covered by `recordDiscovery` and `setHealthy`.
findings.failure_scenario: With three probed local providers, SSE clients get three identical provider events per probe interval.

findings.title: Smoke now opens the production database and skips disabled providers
findings.detail: `main` builds `new Store(cfg.paths.db)`, which runs migrations against the live database from the smoke script. It also now drops disabled providers and turns missing-provider errors into silent skips. Neither change is needed for the requested catalog-not-served check.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the deploy smoke check against new code applies this migration to the live database before the daemon restarts, and a provider that has been disabled is no longer smoke-tested.

findings.title: Daemon won't start after a runtime model is promoted to config.toml or its provider is removed
findings.detail:
Factory's constructor loads `store.runtimeModels()` and throws `catalog collision: ` if the id now exists in code or config, or `unknown provider

` if the provider is gone. Both are normal operator steps: try a model at runtime, then make it permanent in config.toml (and restart, as the GUIDE says), or remove a provider. The next restart then fails. The operator can't fix it with `limitless catalog remove`, because that needs the running daemon's API. The only ways out are editing SQLite by hand or reverting config. A future code release that adds the same model id would brick the daemon the same way.

Result: `Error: catalog collision: mac-mlx/experiment`. Remove the provider from config instead and you get `Error: unknown provider mac-ml

findings.title: DELETE checks only operator cells, so an eval-policy reference to the deleted model breaks the next boot
findings.detail: `remove()` refuses only when `store.routingCells()` names the model. The effective policy also has an eval overlay layer (policy.json, read by `readPolicy` at boot and validated against `this.models`). If that overlay names a runtime model, for example one written by `eval policy --write` after evaluating it, DELETE succeeds. The next Factory construction then throws `Invalid routing policy …`. This is also inconsistent with `patch()`, which validates against the whole effective policy (`router.getPolicy()`).

findings.title: Smoke main now opens the production DB and silently drops checks for disabled providers
findings.detail: To read runtime models, `main()` now opens `new Store(cfg.paths.db)`, which runs migrations on the live database from the smoke process. It also filters every provider check by `getProviderEnabledOverride`, and replaces the 'missing provider' throws with `continue` or `return checks`. If an operator has disabled claude or codex, their whole contract suite (structured, edit, quota, confine…) silently disappears from the deploy smoke instead of reporting a skip. None of this was requested. The task only needed runtime models for the catalog check.

findings.detail: About 520 source lines changed against the ~350 budget, excluding tests. A large share is the smoke.ts restructuring beyond the catalog check itself.

The obvious next step after trying an experiment is to make it permanent with the same id in `[[providers.models]]` (or a release adds that id). That makes the next start throw 'catalog collision'. Removing or renaming the provider in config.toml throws 'unknown provider'. The only supported removal path, `limitless catalog remove`, is an HTTP call to the daemon that just failed to start, so recovery means editing SQLite by hand. findings.title: PATCH cannot clear a runtime model's default effort
findings.detail: `patch` merges `{...old, ...patch}` and re-validates with `modelSchema`. `effort` is `z.enum(...).optional()`, so `effort: null` fails validation, and JSON has no way to send `undefined`. Once a default effort is set it can only be changed to another member of `efforts`. You can't remove it, and you can't narrow `efforts` below it. The workaround is delete and re-add, which DELETE refuses while any policy cell names the model. The GUIDE says agent roles on local Claude-backed servers should omit the default effort, so this is a realistic edit.

findings.title: Smoke now silently drops checks for disabled providers and opens the production DB
findings.detail: `main()` now opens `new Store(cfg.paths.db)`, which runs migrations against the live database, and filters every provider through `getProviderEnabledOverride`. `backendChecks` changed from throwing on a missing provider to `continue` / `return checks`. A provider the operator disabled at runtime (claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter, typesafe) therefore gets no check and no skip row in the deploy smoke report. That is an unrequested change to the deploy gate: a broken provider that is temporarily disabled passes the smoke check and fails once it is re-enabled. Only the catalog check needed the runtime models.

That is every minute for every probed provider even when nothing changed, and twice when health changes, because `setHealthy`→`persist` already publishes. Each publish also triggers `publishFeed()`. `status()` now runs two SQLite queries through `discovery()`, and it is called per candidate on the invoke hot path (`tracker.status(t.provider)` in context.ts).

findings.title: Daemon fails to start when a stored runtime model collides with a code/config model or its provider is gone
findings.detail:
Factory's constructor loads `store.runtimeModels()` and throws `catalog collision: ` or `unknown provider

` for any stored row that no longer fits the static catalog. The collision check exists at add time, but the static catalog can change later: config.toml edits, a code release that adds the same id, or a provider removed from config. When it does, the whole factory refuses to boot. `limitless catalog remove` goes through the HTTP API, so it can't be used while the daemon is down. The operator's only fix is to edit the `runtime_models` table by hand. Stored rows are also not re-validated (no `runtimeModel()` pass) on load. No test covers a restart after the static catalog changes.

findings.title: Every provider SSE event triggers a full refresh of about 20 requests plus a 7-day stats query
findings.detail: Each `provider` message calls `refresh()`. That runs GET /api/routing, /api/catalog, /api/providers and /api/stats/providers (computeProviderWorkload, a 7-day SQL aggregation), then one preview request per role/cell (16 cells in DEFAULT_POLICY). ProviderTracker publishes provider messages on every slot acquire and release (`hold`), on health probes and on OpenRouter polls. With Setup open on a busy factory this is a steady request storm. findings.detail: The request asks History to show recent routing and catalog changes. Only routing history comes from the server. findings.detail: privateMatches now decodes repeatedly: percent-encoding plus a new `\\+u` Unicode-escape pass, for up to 5 rounds. If the text is still changing after that, it returns a synthetic entry 0, so checkPrivateText, checkPrivateRange and blob scans block publication even when private-strings.txt is empty. Before this change, an empty denylist never blocked. These functions gate every commit, patch and blob the factory publishes, and the request (MCP tools plus a digest) didn't ask to change them. The extra layers also add up to 6× the text to NFKC-normalize on large diffs.

findings.detail: `textAt` sets `binary: bytes.includes(0) || bytes.includes(Buffer.from("%PDF-"))`. This matches the five bytes anywhere in the blob, not only at the start of a PDF. The user then sees the "binary bytes, such as a NUL" message even though there is no NUL. This change is an example: `src/git/repos.ts` (line 834) and `test/git-integrity.test.ts` (the `%PDF-1.4` fixtures) are both reported as binary by `diffSince` on c033a43..HEAD, with either the base or head code. gold.summary: NUL-free opaque executable content bypasses the allowance after extension matching replaces mode inspection.

findings.title: Text files that contain the literal "%PDF-" are classified as binary and reported as having NUL bytes
findings.detail: textAt sets `binary: bytes.includes(0) || bytes.includes(Buffer.from("%PDF-"))` for every blob, and binary paths are dropped from `raw`. So any edited text source that mentions "%PDF-" anywhere ends up in binaryPaths through the `!afterText.raw.has(path) && !inert.has(path)` branch. The audit then tells the author the file has "binary bytes, such as a NUL". This is why the automated audit flagged both files in this very change: both contain "%PDF-" and neither contains a NUL. It is the same wild-goose chase the request describes, from a different trigger. This predates the diff and is outside the request's scope.

findings.title: Replacing a regular file with a same-blob symlink is no longer flagged
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is also true when the mode changes but the blob ID stays the same. That includes 100644 -> 120000, a regular file replaced by a symlink with identical content. On base this was flagged, misleadingly, as binary content. With the new INERT_MEDIA_PATH guard it passes silently unless the name looks like media. New symlinks and symlinks with a changed target were never flagged on base either, so this is not a new hole. It is only an incidental check that went away without anyone deciding to remove it.

findings.title: Writing info/exclude fails when the global init.templateDir has no info/ directory
findings.detail: `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That only happens when the template dir has one. With a global `init.templateDir` pointing at a hooks-only template (e.g. the git-secrets setup), `init --bare` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs (verified: `git -c init.templateDir=$TMPDIR/empty init --bare tdt` gives no info/). The redirect fails, and under `set -e` the script exits with a raw shell 'No such file or directory' instead of a generic refusal. It fails safe, but no land can succeed for that user. The #401 push repo never wrote under info/, so this is new.

findings.detail: The `checks:pager` scenario plants `core.pager` and `pager.status`, but the script captures status output with `dirty="$(...)"`, and the test runs without a pseudo-terminal. Git only starts a pager when stdout is a terminal, so no marker could run even with the old in-clone status or with `--no-pager` removed. The request asked for a pseudo-terminal or, failing that, an assertion that `GIT_PAGER` or `--no-pager` is used. The test does neither, so removing the new `--no-pager` from `safe_git` would not fail any test. Only the general 'post-check git uses the private dir' assertion covers isolation here.

findings.title: Writing `info/exclude` fails when git init uses an empty template directory
findings.detail: The line `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That directory comes from the init template. With an empty template (for example a global `init.templateDir` pointing at an empty directory, or `--template=`), `info/` does not exist. I confirmed that `git init --bare --template=` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs. The redirect then fails, `set -e` aborts the land with a raw shell error, and this step skips the script's usual checked-step handling with a generic message.
findings.failure_scenario: A user whose global gitconfig sets `init.templateDir` to an empty directory runs `scripts/land-pr.sh`. The land aborts with 'No such file or directory' after the checks pass.

findings.title: The dirty check still spawns git inside populated submodules, which applies their own config
findings.detail: `status` in the private repository recurses into any gitlink whose directory holds a `.git`, running `git status` there. That child process reads the submodule's own config. `safe_git` only blanks `filter.*` and `hook.*` keys found in the private repository's config, so a `filter.<x>.clean` planted in the submodule's config still runs. I reproduced this: a populated submodule with `filter.x.clean = "touch MARKER; cat"` and a matching attribute created MARKER during `status --porcelain` from an isolated bare repository. The old in-clone status had the same behaviour, and the audit flags gitlinks unless submodules are allowed, so the risk is limited. Still, the request's claim that filter conf
findings.failure_scenario: A PR commits a gitlink `sub`. Its checks run `git init sub` and set `filter.x.clean` in `sub/.git/config`, plus an `info/attributes` file matching a file in `sub`. The post-check status then runs the clean command.

findings.title: Fresh index without stat data makes smudged LFS files look modified
findings.detail: After `read-tree`, the private index has no stat data, so `status` hashes every work-tree file. `safe_git` blanks every `filter.*` key, including the global `filter.lfs.*` ones, so files that LFS smudged on checkout hash to their real contents, not their pointer blobs. They therefore show as modified and the land is refused. The old in-clone status used an index with cached stat data and would not have hashed them. This repository has no tracked `.gitattributes` or LFS files today, so there is no current impact.
findings.failure_scenario: A clone with an LFS-tracked file checked out through the global git-lfs smudge filter runs land-pr.sh. The land is refused with 'Worktree differs from landing commit'.

findings.title: `local` crashes on hosts that don't form a valid URL; provider matching depends on the SSH host matching the base_url origin
findings.detail: `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` throws a TypeError for valid SSH destinations such as a bare IPv6 address (`fe80::1`) or values with spaces, so `limitless local status` exits with a stack trace. Separately, the remote provider is found only by an exact origin match: `http://<remote_host>:8080` against `openaiBaseUrl`. If the SSH alias differs from the base_url host (an alias vs. an IP), or the provider uses `user@host` or https, nothing matches. The health probe then falls back to `http://<host>:8080/v1/models` without the API key, so it reports "unreachable", and up/down never toggle enablement. OPERATIONS.md documents the matching rule, but the failure is silent.
findings.failure_scenario: `[local] remote_host = "gpu"` (an ssh alias), with the provider's `base_url` set to `http://10.0.0.5:8080/v1` and an API key: `local up` reports endpoint unreachable and never enables the provider.

findings.title: Docs still say the llama-server binary lives in `~/.local/share/limitless/llama-bin/`, but the generated unit now defaults to `/usr/local/bin/llama-server`
findings.detail: `remoteUnit`'s default binary changed from the owner's home path to `/usr/local/bin/llama-server`. The remote-host bullet in OPERATIONS still says the binary is a copy in `~/.local/share/limitless/llama-bin/`. On that documented setup, a fresh `local up` without `remote_llama_binary` writes a unit that points to a nonexistent binary.
findings.failure_scenario: A host set up as documented, with no `remote_llama_binary` configured: the generated unit's ExecStart fails because `/usr/local/bin/llama-server` does not exist.

gold.summary: Removing a built-in model leaves persisted routing overrides unable to load at startup.
A runtime model attached to a retired provider prevents factory construction.
Historical run references prevent unrelated catalog mutations.

findings.title: Unguarded new URL() crashes `limitless local` for IPv6 or otherwise invalid remote_host
findings.detail: manageLocal builds `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` with no error handling. If `remote_host` is an IPv6 literal (a valid ssh target) or contains a character URLs reject, the call throws TypeError: Invalid URL. The whole command then fails, including the oMLX report that was already computed. Before this change, a bad host only made the remote endpoint report "unreachable", because fetch errors were caught.
findings.failure_scenario: Set `[local] remote_host = "fd00::5"` and run `limitless local status`. Calling manageLocal('status', {remoteHost: 'fd00::5', ...}) under bun throws `TypeError: Invalid URL`; I ran this.

findings.title: Link to the LAN provider example points at the wrong GUIDE heading
findings.detail: OPERATIONS links to `GUIDE.md#providers-1`. In GUIDE.md the first 'Providers' heading is `### Providers` (line 472, slug `providers`), and that is where the new LAN llama.cpp example lives. The second is `## Providers` (line 1058, slug `providers-1`), which is the general config reference without the LAN example.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader follows the OPERATIONS link to find the matching LAN provider config and lands on the general providers section, which has no LAN llama.cpp example.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: Any unknown stored prefer entry is now silently dropped and mislabelled as a 'retired reference'
findings.detail: `retiredReason(id, providers)` treats every prefer entry that is not a provider id as retired. That includes a model id stored by mistake, such as "codex/sol". Before this change startup refused it with a helpful message ('is a model ID, not a provider; prefer takes provider IDs (use "codex")'). Now it is filtered out and the warning says 'retired reference: codex/sol is not in the catalog', which is false because codex/sol is in the catalog as a model. The base test assertions for this case and for the history count were deleted rather than adapted.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release stored routing.prefer = ["codex/sol"]. On startup the preference is dropped with the warning 'codex/sol: unavailable (retired reference: codex/sol is not in the catalog); prefer', which misleads the operator about the cause.

findings.title: Stored evals and run retries that name the removed model still cannot be resumed
findings.detail: The request says records written before the change 'still render and resume'. Eval resume re-validates the stored request and returns 400 'unknown model ID' for the removed model, and the new test asserts that failure. `Factory.retryRun` also re-validates inherited `run.models`. A historical run pinned to `[retired, live]` fails to retry with `models.implement entry "retired-lan/legacy": Error: unknown model ID`, which I reproduced with a probe test. Interrupted runs do resume, because the router skips unknown ids. This matches how earlier removed models (codex/astra) were handled, so it is not a regression, but it is weaker than the request's wording.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted eval whose request is ["<removed model>@none", "codex/sol@low"] cannot be resumed. A failed run pinned with implement=["<removed model>", "codex/sol"] cannot be retried without new explicit pins.

findings.title: remote_host is parsed as a URL, so some SSH destination forms crash or never match a provider
findings.detail: `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` throws on some SSH destination forms, e.g. `gpu:2222` or `ssh://gpu:2222`, and the CLI exits with an uncaught 'TypeError: Invalid URL'. When remote_host is an SSH alias that differs from the provider's URL host (an ~/.ssh/config alias vs an IP), no provider matches. The health probe then runs without authentication and reports 'unreachable', and up/down silently skip the enable/disable toggle. Enablement matching is documented in OPERATIONS.md, but the crash is not handled.
findings.failure_scenario: With `[local] remote_host = "gpu:2222"`, `limitless local status` throws TypeError: Invalid URL. I confirmed this with `bun -e` against manageLocal.

findings.title: Catalog-edit validation was relaxed beyond retired references, and the change is over budget
findings.detail: `apply()` now validates only references to the edited id that were valid before the edit. Every other already-invalid reference is ignored, not just retired ones, in all layers: code, evals, operator and runs. The test 'catalog POST refuses a retained invalid %s reference' was inverted to 'tolerates'. Re-adding a model under an id that stored chains already reference skips validating those chains, because they were invalid before the add. Together with the Setup.tsx UI additions and the new `unavailable` snapshot fields, source changes are about 250 lines against the requested ~120.
findings.failure_scenario: A stored run chain names "codex/x@high" while codex/x does not exist. An operator POSTs a runtime model codex/x that supports only ["none"]. The add succeeds without checking the run chain, which now holds an unsupported effort that is only discovered when routing.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: Generic retired-ID filtering also silences previously explicit startup errors (owner-decision removals, model-id-in-prefer)
findings.detail: Unknown IDs in stored operator cells and prefer lists are now dropped with a generic warning. That is the fallback the request asked for, but it also replaces two earlier errors. A stored cell naming a model in `REMOVED_MODELS` (for example `claude/fable`) used to stop startup with that model's owner-decision explanation. Now it is dropped silently, with only the warning 'retired reference: claude/fable is not in the catalog'. A stored prefer containing a model ID (`codex/sol`) used to stop startup with a fix-it hint ('prefer takes provider IDs (use "codex")'). Now it is filtered out silently. The test that covered both messages was deleted rather than adapted.
findings.failure_scenario: A database has `prefer = ["codex/sol"]` from an older release. After upgrading, prefer silently becomes empty instead of showing the hint to use `codex`. Because operatorPrefer is non-null and empty, it also overrides the config's preferProviders.

findings.title: Malformed `[local].remote_host` crashes `limitless local` with a bare 'Invalid URL'
findings.detail: `manageLocal` now runs `new URL(\`http://${host}:8080\`)` to find the matching provider. A host value that isn't a valid URL host (a space, an `ssh://` form, or `host:port`) throws a TypeError before any SSH call. The user sees only 'Invalid URL', which doesn't mention `remote_host`. The old code never parsed the host as a URL.
findings.failure_scenario: I set `[local] remote_host = "bad host"` and ran `limitless local status`. Output: 'Invalid URL'.

findings.title: Remote provider is matched only by an openaiBaseUrl origin on port 8080
findings.detail: `local up` and `local down` find the provider whose `openaiBaseUrl` origin equals `http://<remote_host>:8080`. This breaks in three cases: a LAN provider configured through `ssh_forward` (base URL on 127.0.0.1), one with a different hostname or IP spelling than `remote_host`, or an anthropic-compatible provider (`baseUrl` only). In all three, no provider is matched. Then the health probe goes out without the API key, so llama-server answers 401 and the endpoint shows 'unreachable', and enablement is never updated. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` documents the limitation, but the failure is silent.
findings.failure_scenario: The config defines a `lan` provider with `base_url = "http://192.168.1.5:8080/v1"` and `[local].remote_host = "gpu-box"`. `local up` starts the unit but reports endpoint unreachable (401) and never enables `lan`.

findings.title: Smoke no longer covers any LAN llama.cpp provider
findings.detail: `backendChecks` still loops over a fixed list of provider ids, now `['omlx', 'openrouter']`. Removing the machine-named entry means a config-defined LAN llama.cpp provider, which the docs now present as the supported route, never gets a structured-output smoke check. The removed provider previously got one when healthy.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configures `lan` as in `docs/GUIDE.md`. `limitless deploy --smoke` never exercises it, so a broken chat template on the LAN server isn't caught.

findings.title: Over the ~120-line source budget, partly from extra scope
findings.detail: About 260 lines of source changed against the requested budget of about 120. Requirement 4 justifies the retired-reference filtering in `retired.ts`, `runtime-policy.ts` and `runtime-catalog.ts`. The new `unavailable` listing in the routing snapshot and the Setup UI rendering go beyond what the request asked for.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime defect; more code to review and maintain.

findings.title: `limitless local` crashes on an IPv6 or host:port remote_host
findings.detail: `manageLocal` now runs `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` to find the matching provider. That throws a TypeError for an IPv6 literal (e.g. `fe80::1`) or a value that includes a port, so the whole command fails, including the oMLX report already built. Before the change the host was only put into a URL string, and a failing fetch was caught and reported as `unreachable`.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran `bun probe.ts` calling `manageLocal('status', { remoteHost: 'fe80::1', ... })`. Output: `fe80::1 THROWS TypeError: Invalid URL`. The same happens for `remoteHost: 'box:22'`.

findings.title: Persisted routing cells naming removed models are now silently dropped, and the test that guarded the old behavior was deleted
findings.detail: Before this change, startup threw if a persisted operator cell named an explicitly removed model (e.g. `claude/fable`, which has an owner-decision entry in REMOVED_MODELS). The error carried that owner-decision reason. Startup also threw a helpful 'is a model ID, not a provider' error for a model id stored in `prefer`. Now `filterRetiredTargets` and the `retiredReason` prefer filter quietly drop both cases with a generic 'retired reference: X is not in the catalog' warning. The old test (`startup validates persisted operator cells and preferences against today's catalog`) was replaced by one that only checks an invalid effort.
findings.failure_scenario: The store has `triage.default = ['claude/fable']`. Before: startup failed, naming the owner decision. Now: startup succeeds, triage quietly falls back to the code/evals policy, and the warning only says it is 'not in the catalog'.

findings.title: Scope is well over budget and changes catalog-removal rules beyond the request
findings.detail:
About 280 lines of source changed against a budget of about 120. The extras:
- a new `unavailable` diagnostics field in the routing and catalog snapshots, with credential-redaction plumbing
- new UI in `ui/pages/Setup.tsx`
- the `remove()` check that blocked removing a runtime model referenced by operator cells was deleted; the scoped operator-layer validation now covers that
- a new rule lets a runtime model be removed even when finished runs reference it

The scoping itself is needed so that runs and cells naming retired ids don't block every catalog edit. The rule change for finished runs and the UI diagnostics were not requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model referenced only by a finished run can now be deleted. Before the change that edit was rejected.

findings.title: Reading `[local].remote_*` from config.toml is not tested end to end
findings.detail: The request asks for tests of `limitless local status` with and without `[local].remote_host`. The new tests call `manageLocal` directly with `remoteHost` set or unset. The CLI code in `src/cli/main.ts` that turns `local.remote_host`, `remote_model_path` and `remote_llama_binary` into those options is not exercised; only `--help` output is checked. Old `twilight_*` keys are now silently ignored, also untested and with no warning.
findings.failure_scenario: If `main.ts` read `local.remoteHost` instead of `local.remote_host`, every test would still pass while `limitless local status` would ignore the configured host.
