findings.title: Retrying a pre-change run whose chain pins the removed model fails
findings.detail: Requirement 4 says records written before the change must render and resume. Stored routing cells and preferences are now filtered generically, but retryRun passes the inherited run.models through createRun -> validateRunModels. That validator still rejects unknown model ids, so a run that pinned the machine-named model (or any removed id) cannot be retried. The retryRun comment already says inherited chains 'predate this constraint', and they could be filtered with filterRetiredTargets the same way persisted operator cells are.
findings.failure_scenario: Store a failed run with models {triage: ["retired-lan/legacy@none", "openrouter/gpt-6-luna@none"]} and call factory.retryRun(run.id). Observed: throws 'models.triage entry "retired-lan/legacy@none": Error: unknown model ID "retired-lan/legacy"' (checked with a test written for this review).

findings.title: Unrequested relaxation: catalog removal now ignores pins in terminal runs
findings.detail: apply() now skips terminal runs when model === null, and the existing test 'catalog validates stored chains beyond the default run limit and regardless of status' was replaced with one asserting removal succeeds for finished runs. The new 'affected' scoping already stops stale or retired references from blocking edits, so this extra relaxation is not needed for the request. It also creates more runs that cannot be retried (see the retry finding).
findings.failure_scenario: Add runtime model codex/x, create a succeeded run pinning codex/x@high, then DELETE /api/catalog/models/codex%2Fx: it now returns 200 (before: 400). Retrying that run then fails with unknown model ID.

findings.title: `limitless local` throws on an IPv6 remote_host
findings.detail: manageLocal builds `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` without brackets. For a bare IPv6 literal (e.g. remote_host = "fe80::1"), URL construction throws a TypeError. That aborts the whole command, including the oMLX report that is already computed. The old code never parsed the host.
findings.failure_scenario: [local] remote_host = "fe80::1"; `limitless local status` exits with 'TypeError: Invalid URL' instead of reporting oMLX and remote status.

findings.title: Source diff is well over the stated budget
findings.detail: Source, script and UI changes total +194/-95 lines, against a budget of about 120 lines that were meant to be mostly deletions. The extra lines are new code: unavailable-target diagnostics with credential redaction in RuntimePolicy/RuntimeCatalog, new Setup.tsx output, and a new retired.ts module. Not wrong, but it widens the review surface beyond the rename and removal that were requested.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure; the extra code makes the change harder to review and maintain.

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Line-by-line redaction of failure excerpts misses credentials that contain a newline
findings.detail: The coverage and failure-excerpt collectors receive output one line at a time, and each line is redacted on its own. If a registered credential contains a newline (for example a multi-line key), no single line contains the full value, so each piece passes through unredacted into `failures`. The `combined` tail does not have this problem because it is redacted as a whole. Today credentials come only from `src/config.ts` secrets, which are typically single-line tokens, so this is unlikely in practice.
findings.failure_scenario: A multi-line credential (such as a PEM private key) is registered, and a failing test prints it just before a `(fail)` line. The stored `failures` field then contains the key's lines unredacted, and they reach implementer feedback.

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Baseline cache entries from before redaction are still reused
findings.detail: Redaction changes what a stored GateResult contains, but GATE_ENV_VERSION (whose comment says to bump it when result shape or execution changes) was not bumped. Passing baselines cached before this change keep their unredacted output for up to BASELINE_CACHE_TTL_MS (7 days). engine.ts reuses them and copies them into the new run's baseline-gates.json artifact and gate events, so unredacted gate text written before the upgrade keeps being re-stored after it.
findings.failure_scenario: A baseline check that passes but prints a registered credential is cached before the upgrade. After upgrading, a run on the same base SHA hits the cache, and the raw credential is written into that run's baseline-gates.json artifact and its gate event data.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Change is far over its budget and redacts at many consumers instead of once at the source
findings.detail: The request said: redact gate output once, where `runGates` builds the result, about 30 net source lines, so every consumer gets redacted text from one place. The diff changes about 115 source lines. On top of the source fix it adds: `redactGateData` (a JSON round-trip that also rewrites objects) applied to every HTTP JSON and SSE payload; re-serialization of the artifact endpoint; redaction of `RunContext` state in the constructor; redaction in `renderReport`, `implementPrompt`, `reviewPrompt`, `verifyPrompt` and `formatGateOutput`; per-stream truncation flags in `ProcResult`; and new `confinementError` semantics (now always written, and when it is false, `confinementFailed` no longer scans
findings.failure_scenario: Any reviewer comparing the diff against the issue: 18 files and about 115 source lines changed against a stated budget of about 30, with changes to the API and run state that the issue did not ask for.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint now rewrites stored artifacts (minifies JSON, adds fields, strips control sequences)
findings.detail: `redactGateArtifact` parses every artifact as JSON and re-serializes it through `redactGateData`. Pretty-printed artifacts such as `baseline-gates.json` and `gates-N.json` (written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)`) are now served minified. Any object that has `ok` and `output` also gets a `confinementError` field that was never stored. Artifacts that are not JSON (`diff.patch`, `report.md`, `spec.md`) go through `stripVTControlCharacters`, so the patch served is not byte-identical to the stored one. Probe output: `{"checks":[{"name":"t","ok":true,"output":"fine","confinementError":false}]}` from a pretty-printed input without that field.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json returns one minified line with an added confinementError field instead of the stored pretty-printed JSON. GET …/diff.patch on a change that adds ESC sequences returns a patch without them.

findings.title: Review prompt input is ANSI-stripped, so the reviewer sees a different patch than the one under review
findings.detail: `reviewPrompt` now runs its whole input through `redactGateData`, which applies `stripVTControlCharacters` to every string, including the inline `patch`, the request `prompt` and the implementer report. Terminal escape sequences that a change adds to source or fixtures disappear from the diff the reviewer reads. A reviewer can then neither see nor flag them, e.g. terminal-injection content in output strings. This goes beyond gate output, which was the only scope of the request.
findings.failure_scenario: Under PR verification, a diff adds `console.log("\x1b]0;pwned\x07")` as raw ESC/BEL bytes. The patch in the review prompt shows the line without the escape sequence, so the reviewer approves what looks like a harmless log line.

findings.title: `confinementError` now always serialized, reversing the documented 'present only when set' convention
findings.detail: The removed comment said the field was 'Present only when set, like timedOut, so results stay readable by strict schemas and older releases.' Every result now carries `confinementError: false`, and `confinementFailed` uses `??`, so an explicit false overrides the output scan. Both changes support the 'redaction could hide the diagnostic' edge case, which the raw line scan already covered without changing what is persisted.
findings.failure_scenario: A tool with a strict schema for gate results, of the kind the removed comment warned about, rejects rows that now carry `confinementError: false`.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.

findings.title: Redaction spread to every HTTP/SSE response, state load and prompt input, beyond the single-point design and ~30-line budget
findings.detail: The request asks for gate output to be redacted once, where runGates builds a check result, in about 30 source lines. The change adds about 100 net source lines and also runs redactGateData in other places: on all JSON responses and SSE messages (http.ts serialize), on RunContext state when it loads, on cached stage values, on the whole implement/review/verify prompt inputs and on renderReport. redactGateData is a JSON round trip that strips terminal colour codes from every string. It also adds `confinementError` to any object that has both `ok` and `output` keys, gate result or not. All of this goes well past the request's scope.
findings.failure_scenario: In a quick benchmark, serialising 20,000 events through json() went from 16 ms to 137 ms. Any API object shaped like {ok: true, output: "..."} comes back with an extra confinementError field, and any string with colour codes comes back without them.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint rewrites stored content (diff.patch, pretty JSON)
findings.detail: redactGateArtifact runs on every artifact the endpoint returns, not just gate artifacts. Non-JSON artifacts such as diff.patch go through redactGateOutput, which removes escape sequences and replaces registered-credential strings. JSON artifacts are parsed and written back out compactly. The bytes returned no longer match what was stored.
findings.failure_scenario: A change adds a file with literal ESC bytes (a terminal fixture). GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/diff.patch returns a patch without those bytes, so it no longer applies or matches the reviewed change.

findings.title: Unrequested change hides MCP and digest text that contains "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any text that contains the literal "[redacted]". Before, it ran redactCredentials and returned the text. This is the privacy filter for MCP tools, MCP status and the digest CLI. The issue rules out changing other output paths, and no test in the diff covers this. Every place that already redacts (harness tool results, and now gate output) leaves that marker in stored text, so a field that was partly redacted before is now hidden entirely. That includes run errors, land reasons and titles. Nothing in the diff explains why the change is needed.
findings.failure_scenario: A run's error or land reason contains a gate excerpt such as "error: token [redacted] rejected". `limitless digest` or the MCP run-status tool now shows "[withheld: private text]" instead of the useful redacted message.

findings.detail: The request asked for redaction once, where runGates builds a result, and in the deploy gate. The diff also wraps every HTTP JSON response, every SSE message and every artifact in redactGateData or redactGateOutput. It does the same for RunState in the RunContext constructor, check-cache hits, renderReport input, and the input to implementPrompt, reviewPrompt and verifyPrompt. redactGateData also strips terminal control codes from every string, including user prompts, PR patches and diff.patch artifacts. It adds a `confinementError` field to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys, whether or not it is a gate result. Every response is serialized twice. Together this is roughly 100 net sou

findings.title: FailureExcerpts is about 17x slower and no longer caps line length
findings.detail: After 39 lines, every new line causes the whole window to be joined and redacted again. The 8,000-character cap per line was removed, so up to 39 lines of any length are kept and rejoined on each push. In runOne each line is also redacted before observe, inside observe, and again at finish. This runs synchronously in the process's data handlers on the shared daemon's event loop. Benchmark of extractFailures with 6 registered credentials (`bun $TMPDIR/bench/b.ts <root>`), base vs HEAD: 200k ordinary lines took 43 ms vs 731 ms; 2,000 lines of 200 KB each took 511 ms vs 6,699 ms.
findings.failure_scenario: A failing test suite prints hundreds of thousands of lines, or a few very long minified lines. The gate run spends seconds of synchronous CPU redacting the same text repeatedly, which delays HTTP and SSE handling in the factory daemon.

findings.title: MCP/digest privacy filter now withholds any text that contains the literal "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing "[redacted]". The request did not ask for this, and no added test covers it. Gate output, land reasons and errors now normally carry the redaction marker after this change, so explainStatus (mcp-status.ts) and the digest (digest.ts) blank out whole fields instead of showing the redacted text. The same happens to any run title or prompt that just mentions "[redacted]" (e.g. an issue about redaction like this one). That loses information in an unrelated subsystem.

findings.title: FailureExcerpts lost its per-line cap and re-redacts the whole window on every line (≈19x slower)
findings.detail: The old code capped each retained line at 8,000 chars and used a simple shift. The new code keeps lines at full length. Once the window is full, every further diagnostic line triggers join + redactCredentials + split over ~40 lines, and each line is already redacted twice before that (in run.ts observe and again in observe()). All of this runs synchronously in the line callbacks on the factory's event loop, and retained lines are no longer bounded in memory.

findings.detail: json() and the SSE send now run redactGateData on every response. The same deep round trip was added to implementPrompt, reviewPrompt, verifyPrompt, renderReport and the RunContext constructor. findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json returns compact JSON where it used to return the stored 2-space-indented JSON. redactGateData({ok:true,output:'hi'}) adds confinementError:false to unrelated API objects.

findings.title: Truncation overlap ignores the longer JSON-escaped credential variants
findings.detail: redactGateStreams drops `secret.length - 1` chars after a runner cut. But registerCredential now also redacts JSON-escaped variants, which can be longer, e.g. a secret with newlines or quotes. If the cut lands inside an escaped variant, a suffix longer than the overlap can survive.
findings.failure_scenario: The secret contains several quote or newline characters. A gate prints JSON.stringify(secret) past the 64 KB runner tail, and the cut lands near the start of the escaped form. The remaining suffix is longer than secret.length-1, so part of it is kept.

gold.summary: Redacting the carry early emits suffixes of overlapping registered credentials.
ANSI stripping after framing and tail cuts leaves accidental credential fragments visible.

findings.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text containing the literal "[redacted]"
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing "[redacted]", whatever its source. The filter is shared by the MCP tools (mcp.ts, mcp-status.ts) and the digest CLI. Harnesses already redact credentials to "[redacted]" in agent tool results and errors, and gate output now does too. So run errors, feedback, terminal reasons and events that used to show their redacted text are now hidden entirely. So is any user prompt that contains the literal token. The request did not ask for this, it lists other command output as out of scope, and no test in the diff covers it.
findings.failure_scenario: I called `loadOutputPrivacy()("Gate test failed: see logs. Tip: values shown as [redacted] were hidden")` and it returned "[withheld: private text]". With base code it returned the text unchanged. A run whose gate feedback contains a redacted credential now shows its whole feedback field as withheld

findings.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts and strips control sequences from patches
findings.detail: `redactGateArtifact` runs `JSON.parse` and then `JSON.stringify` with no indent on every artifact that parses as JSON. It also passes the data through `redactGateData`, which adds a `confinementError` field to every object that has `ok` and `output` keys. Artifacts written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` (gates-N.json, baseline-gates.json, review-shadow artifacts) are now served as one compact line with extra fields. Text artifacts such as diff.patch go through `stripVTControlCharacters`, so the served patch can differ from the stored one. The same VT stripping applies to the inline `patch` given to `reviewPrompt` through `redactGateData(input)`.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json used to return indented JSON and now returns a single line with `"confinementError":false` added to each result. A diff.patch that adds a fixture containing raw ESC bytes is served without them, so it no longer applies cleanly.

findings.title: Scope well beyond the request: redaction of every HTTP/SSE response and of run state
findings.detail: The request asked for one redaction point in runGates plus the deploy gate, about 30 net source lines. The change adds about 115 net source lines. It round-trips every JSON response and SSE message through `redactGateData`, which strips VT sequences, redacts all strings and injects `confinementError` into any object shaped like `{ok, output}`. It also rewrites the whole RunState on every RunContext construction (context.ts:306) and re-redacts in each prompt builder and in renderReport. Each of these runs a full JSON serialize and parse on every call, and each changes data the request did not cover. The added code is hard to tell apart from the one place that actually matters.
findings.failure_scenario: Every /api/runs, /api/feed and SSE message pays a second full JSON round trip. Any non-gate object with `ok` and `output` keys gains a `confinementError` field in API responses.

findings.title: Unused per-stream truncation flags added to ProcResult
findings.detail: `stdoutTruncated` and `stderrTruncated` are computed and returned, but nothing in src reads them. Only the new tests in hardening.test.ts and proc.test.ts check them.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime failure. The public ProcResult type grows two fields nothing uses, so more code has to be maintained.

findings.title: MCP/digest privacy filter now withholds any text containing the literal "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains "[redacted]". It used to pass already-redacted text through. This affects every MCP tool result (through privateOutputData) and every digest line or error. Any field that legitimately contains the redaction marker loses its whole content, and so does user-written text that contains the literal. Examples are run errors, gate output, and agent tool results already redacted by the harnesses. No test covers the change, and the request does not ask for it.
findings.failure_scenario: I checked this with a script: `loadOutputPrivacy()("Check test failed: error: credential [redacted]\n(fail) assertion foo.test.ts")` returns `[withheld: private text]`. Before the change it returned the text unchanged. So an MCP status query for a run whose gate output had a credential redacted lose

findings.title: reviewPrompt VT-strips the inline patch, so reviewers cannot see escape sequences that an external PR introduces
findings.detail: `input = redactGateData(input)` runs stripVTControlCharacters over every string in the review input. That includes `patch`, which is inlined for PR verification of external, untrusted changes. Raw ESC/CSI sequences added by the change, such as terminal-injection or concealment codes in source files, are silently removed from what the reviewer sees. The verify prompt and the artifact endpoint do the same.
findings.failure_scenario: An external PR adds `\x1b[8m` (conceal) or cursor-movement sequences to a source file. The patch shown inline in the review prompt has them stripped, so the reviewer has no evidence to flag them.

findings.title: confinementError is now always written and output is VT-stripped, which changes how an older release reads new results
findings.detail: The removed comment said confinementError was 'present only when set … so results stay readable by … older releases'. It is now always written, and `output` is now VT-stripped. An older release reads `!!confinementError || output.includes(marker)`. For output whose raw text was `Oper\x1b[0mation`, the new version records confinementError: false. After stripping, the stored output contains the full marker, so an older release reading the row would classify it as a confinement error. This only matters on rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: New code stores {confinementError:false, output:"sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted"} from a check that printed an ANSI-interrupted marker. After a rollback, the older release marks the check as a confinement error.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Deploy gate redaction does nothing in production: the deploy CLI process never registers credentials
findings.detail: The `deploy` case in src/cli/main.ts imports ./service.ts and calls svc.deploy without calling loadConfig(). registerCredential is called only from src/config.ts:182 (inside loadConfig), and neither service.ts nor its imports load config. So in a real `limitless deploy` process the credential set is empty, and both `redactOutput: true` and `redactGateStreams` return the text unchanged. The deploy error still contains any provider API key a check prints. The new deploy tests call registerCredential themselves in the test process, which hides the gap.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless deploy --smoke`. A test in the release checkout fails and prints the provider API key from the environment or a fixture. registeredCredentials() is empty in that CLI process, so the thrown deploy error and the console show the key unredacted.

findings.detail: The issue asks for gate output to be redacted once, where runGates builds a check's result, so that every consumer receives redacted text from that one place. The budget is about 30 net source lines. The diff adds 140 net source lines and also redacts in: every HTTP JSON response and SSE message (`serialize`), the artifact endpoint (re-parsing and re-serializing every artifact), RunContext state on load, checkpoint reads, implementPrompt, reviewPrompt, verifyPrompt, formatGateFeedback, renderReport and formatGateOutput. It also adds JSON-escaped credential variants, per-stream truncation flags and a change to the MCP privacy policy. AGENTS.md says to stay within the issue's line budget and t
findings.failure_scenario: Every API response and SSE event is now stringified, parsed and stringified again, with every string VT-stripped and scanned for credentials. That is extra cost and behavior change on all endpoints, for a request that only covered gate output.

findings.title: MCP/digest privacy now hides any text containing "[redacted]", with no test
findings.detail: `text.includes("[redacted]")` now replaces the whole string with "[withheld: private text]". Harness-redacted agent output, run titles or review findings that mention the marker, and gate output that is now redacted all lose their full text in MCP tools and the digest. Before, they passed through with only the credential replaced. No test was added for this policy change.
findings.failure_scenario: A run's gate output is "credential: [redacted]\n(fail) assertion ...". An MCP client reading the run's gates gets "[withheld: private text]" in place of the whole diagnostic.

findings.title: redactGateData strips terminal control characters from every string and adds confinementError to unrelated payloads
findings.detail: redactGateData is now applied to all HTTP responses, non-JSON artifacts (for example diff.patch, through redactGateOutput), the review prompt's inline patch and the user prompt. It strips VT control characters from all of them, which changes content beyond credential redaction. It also adds `confinementError` to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys, whether or not it is a GateResult.
findings.failure_scenario: A patch that adds a file containing literal ESC bytes is served by /api/runs/:id/artifacts/diff.patch with those bytes removed, so it no longer applies cleanly.

Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Output privacy filter now withholds any text containing "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains the literal "[redacted]". Before, it would redact the string and return it. The request did not ask for this, and no test covers it. MCP status/tools and the digest pass all free text through this filter. So any event message, gate excerpt or report that this change (or the harnesses) already redacted is now hidden completely. The filter is also no longer idempotent: applying it to its own redacted output withholds everything.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe: loadOutputPrivacy()("build failed; see [redacted] token note") returns "[withheld: private text]". Any gate failure that once printed a credential is fully hidden from MCP get_status/digest, not shown with the value masked.

findings.title: Large out-of-scope rewrite: HTTP, SSE, artifacts, run state and reports all pass through redactGateData; budget exceeded about 6x
findings.detail: The request asked to redact once where runGates builds a result, plus the deploy tails, in about 30 net source lines. The source diff adds about 180 net lines. It also sends every HTTP JSON response, every SSE message, every artifact body, the whole RunState (context.ts constructor), checkpoint cache reads, renderReport input and the whole implement/review/verify prompt inputs through a JSON round-trip. That round-trip strips terminal escape sequences from every string, redacts every string, and adds a confinementError field to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys. Most of this goes past the stated out-of-scope line: other output is not gate output. AGENTS.md says to keep to the line b
findings.failure_scenario: Any API consumer now gets responses rewritten by gate-specific logic. Every object with `ok`/`output` gains a `confinementError` key, and escape sequences are removed from unrelated strings such as prompts and patch text in reviewPrompt.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts, losing their formatting
findings.detail: redactGateArtifact parses every artifact as JSON and returns JSON.stringify output with no indentation. Artifacts saved pretty-printed (gates-N.json, baseline-gates.json, review-shadow) are now returned as one long line. The UI's getArtifact displays res.text() directly. Parsing and re-serializing also adds confinementError to gate result objects, and it loses precision on large numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json, stored by JSON.stringify(cmp, null, 2), now returns single-line JSON. That is hard to read in the UI artifact view.

findings.title: confinementError is now always written, reversing the deliberate present-only-when-set format
findings.detail: The old code wrote confinementError only when it was true, with a comment saying this kept results readable by strict schemas and older releases. Now every new GateResult records false or true. This affects cache rows, artifacts, state and events. confinementFailed now treats an explicit false as authoritative and skips the output scan. The current strict eval schema accepts false, so nothing breaks today. Still, the persisted format changed without that being requested, and redactGateData backfills the field into legacy objects.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release, or an external reader that expects the field only when it is true, sees confinementError:false on every stored result after this ships.
